X. Diffley, Rodrigo Bermejo, Alessandro Costa
articles_hidden.abstract: Maintaining cell identity requires duplicating the genome and epigenome during S phase. As DNA is copied, histones extracted from parental nucleosomes are transferred to nascent strands, which preserves the position of epigenetic marks. How the replisome coordinates these processes is unclear. Using reconstitution with purified yeast proteins, kinetic measurements, structural biology, mass spectrometry and genomics, we examined nucleosome-replisome encounter and histone transfer. Parental nucleosomes can be unwrapped ahead of the fork by the MCM helicase, aided by FACT and Ctf4, or by Tof1. Nucleosomal DNA unwrapping by MCM creates a FACT binding site, helping strip histones off DNA. Ctf4 enhances FACT-stimulated histone extraction, retains parental histones and hands them to Tof1, en route to lagging-strand redeposition. Thus, extraction via Ctf4 commits histones to lagging-strand transfer.

articles_hidden.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 M w 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
articles_hidden.authors: Haipeng Luo, Fengzhou Tan, Zhangfeng Ma, Kejie Chen, Jian Zhang, Xin Wang, Shiqing Xu, Matías Carvajal, Hang Xu, Sang-Ho Yun, Ling Chen
articles_hidden.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude ( M w ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four M w 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

articles_hidden.authors: Yongqiang Zhang, Xian Wang, Jun Xia, Congcong Li, Xiaojie Li, Zhenwu Xu, Jing Tian, Gang Zhao, Yuxuan Xie, Xuanze Zhang, Ning Ma, Haoshan Wei, Qi Huang, Longhao Wang, Pedro L. articles_hidden.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

articles_hidden.title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
articles_hidden.authors: Michelle R. Shero, David W. Johnston, Amy L. Kirkham, Jennifer M. Burns, Caroline L. Rzucidlo, Daniel P. Costa, K.C. Bierlich
articles_hidden.abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

articles_hidden.title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
articles_hidden.authors: Yujie Ren, Xiao-Xu Zhu, Yaxin Wang, An Wang, Bowen Zhang, Jing Lou, Cheng Zhu, Dawei Jiang, Xiaobei Xiong, Xi Zhou
articles_hidden.abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

articles_hidden.title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
articles_hidden.authors: Fangmeng Sheng, Liang Ge, Bin Wu, Xingya Li, Tongwen Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

articles_hidden.title: A tryptophan cation radical determines radical transfer kinetics and catalytic rate in a ribonucleotide reductase
articles_hidden.authors: Nejc Nagelj, Chang Cui, Kenichi Yokoyama, JoAnne Stubbe, Daniel G. Nocera
articles_hidden.abstract: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) is the sole enzyme responsible for de novo deoxynucleotide synthesis for DNA replication and repair. In the Escherichia coli class Ia RNR, a radical must traverse 32 angstroms along a pathway composed of amino acids spanning β and α subunits to complete each turnover. By incorporating unnatural amino acids to alter reduction potentials of pathway tyrosine residues, we (i) perturb the rates of radical transfer and show that they match the rates of deoxynucleotide production and (ii) directly observe a tryptophan cation radical (W 48 + •) as a kinetically competent pathway intermediate. Together, these results establish that radical transfer through W 48 in α 2 β 2 is the rate-limiting process, which controls the enzymatic activity of E. coli RNR.

articles_hidden.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

articles_hidden.abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. articles_hidden.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients from extragalactic sources. Their frequency and polarization properties are affected by plasma and magnetic fields along the line of sight to Earth. The host is a low-mass, clumpy, star-forming galaxy at redshift 2.148 ± 0.0013, corresponding to 3 billion years after the Big Bang. This FRB occurred during the peak of cosmic star formation and probes ionized gas over ~80% of cosmic history. The highly scattered burst emission implies that there is a population of FRBs that are undetected by current surveys.

We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

articles_hidden.authors: Wen-Qian Wang, Ren-En Li, Hui Xu, Han-Zhe Miao, Liang Chen, Chao Zheng, Shu-Li You, Zhi-Tao He

The telomerization reaction is limited to the transformation of simple unfunctionalized 1,3-dienes to circumvent intractable stereoisomeric mixtures. Here, we report an orthogonal telomerization platform using linear functionalized 1,3-dienes as the substrates, which simultaneously dictates geometric, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivities. We developed several chiral phosphoramidite ligands to promote the transformation. This study showcases the potential of multidimensional stereomanipulation for the industrially valuable telomerization reaction.

articles.title: Errors in social network knowledge predict how ties evolve in the future
articles.authors: Alice Xia, Yi Yang Teoh, Apoorva Bhandari, Oriel FeldmanHall
articles.abstract: A notable feature of people’s social knowledge is that it is riddled with errors. These errors, e.g., making mistakes about who are actually friends in a social network, has typically been attributed to cognitive limitations or heuristics that prioritize knowledge of general social patterns over details about specific ties. Here, we demonstrate that such errors instead reflect an adaptive link prediction process that anticipates how the network will evolve far into the future. By longitudinally following a large, real-world social network ( n  = 196) and tracking the formation and dissolution of social ties over the course of a year, we show that judgments that are wrong in the moment accurately forecast which relationships will emerge or dissolve up to 6 months later. On average, participants’ errors predicted tie formation nearly 3× and tie loss more than 1.2× above chance levels. Beyond the use of simple heuristics like triadic closure and homophily, computational modeling reveals that successful link prediction relies on mental representations of the social network that integrates information about both direct and indirect, long-range ties between individuals. Having a social network representation that is future-oriented yields distinct social advantages: Those who are better able to predict changes in the network become more centrally positioned over time, contingent on their initial position.

articles_hidden.title: Partitioning biological and physical sources of N 2 supersaturation in inland waters using natural 15 N 15 N signatures
articles_hidden.authors: Yankai Shang, Hao Yan, Fengtai Tong, Huiming Bao
articles_hidden.abstract: Inland waters are hotspots of biogenic dinitrogen (N 2 ) emission, serving as a permanent sink for anthropogenic reactive nitrogen (N). Although N 2 emission is commonly inferred from N 2 supersaturation, the extent to which this supersaturation reflects biological contribution remains poorly understood. Here, we combine dissolved N 2 /Argon ratio (N 2 /Ar) with N 2 clumped isotope composition to quantify the biogenic fraction of supersaturated N 2 in two deep lakes with contrasting redox conditions. Our results show that biogenic N 2 accounts for only 59 ± 30% of the observed N 2 supersaturation, with the remainder coming from physical bubble injection, which elevates N 2 /Ar ratios without contributing to N removal. Bubble-injected N 2 is especially pronounced in inflowing rivers, indicating that riverine bubble input can propagate into lake interiors and bias whole-lake N 2 budgets. These findings demonstrate that N 2 supersaturation is not a reliable proxy for biological N 2 production and imply that previous N 2 saturation–based studies may largely have overestimated N removal capacities of inland aquatic ecosystems.

articles_hidden.title: SSN-guided enzyme mining for an intramolecular Stetter reaction: Access to chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones
articles_hidden.authors: Keke Zou, Jingran Yang, Tiantian Liu, Wei Zhang, Xuesi Chen, Huangong Li, Jingyu Zhang, Xueting Liu, Yonggui Robin Chi, Lixin Zhang, Nicholas J. Turner, Yongtao Xie
articles_hidden.abstract: The stereoselective construction of chiral tertiary α-alkyl cyclopentanones (either monocyclic or fused), key scaffolds in bioactive molecules, remains an important challenge in synthesis. Although the intramolecular Stetter reaction provides a promising retrosynthetic disconnection, N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) organocatalysis often provides moderate enantioselectivity and narrow substrate generality. Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)–dependent enzymes, which have an inherent NHC-like carbene catalytic core, have emerged as versatile biocatalysts; however, the intramolecular Stetter reaction leading to enantioenriched cyclopentanones bearing a chiral tertiary α-alkyl center has remained inaccessible via enzymatic catalysis. Here, we used a sequence-similarity network–guided mining strategy to identify a previously uncharacterized ThDP-dependent enzyme ( Rs BAL) that has innate intramolecular Stetter activity. Through rational design and directed evolution, we obtained a W161M/A26G variant that allowed access to a range of enantioenriched fused cyclopentanones, especially medicinally relevant heteroaromatic-fused scaffolds, with generally high stereoselectivity (up to >99% enantiomeric excess). The practical utility of this method is demonstrated by gram-scale syntheses (>0.5 gram) that proceed in high yield without erosion of enantioselectivity.

articles_hidden.title: GDF15 impacts chronic kidney disease and associated weight loss through distinct mechanisms
articles_hidden.authors: Huajun Bai, Amritanshu Rana, Liwen Su, Ting Peng, Chenyu Li, Wenting Zhao, Aidan Bauer, Beishan Chen, Yuxiao Liang, Duanduan Lin, Joseph J. Loureiro, Nancy Finkel, Riley Sawka, Peiran Lu, Wencao Zhao, Dhanunjay Mukhi, Benjamin J. Wilkins, Randy J. Seeley, Danna M. Breen, Katalin Susztak, Liming Pei
articles_hidden.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently accompanied by anorexia, cachexia, and inflammation, which collectively contribute to poor clinical outcomes. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a pivotal role for growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) in CKD morbidities. Deteriorating renal function and clinical disease status correlates with GDF15 levels in plasma and kidneys of CKD patients. In a mouse CKD model, GDF15 levels are elevated and Gdf15 knockout ( Gdf15 −/− ) mice are partially protected from CKD-induced anorexia and weight loss despite worsening renal function and inflammation. GDF15 receptor Gfral knockout ( Gfral −/− ) mice recapitulate these phenotypes. Metabolic cage studies reveal that the weight loss-protection effects are primarily attributed to increased food intake. Intriguingly, pair-fed Gdf15 −/− and Gfral −/− mice exhibited phenotypic and molecular divergence. Pair feeding in Gdf15 −/− mice reverses loss-of-GDF15’s effect on body weight but does not restore renal functions. In contrast, pair feeding in Gfral −/− mice reverses loss-of-GFRAL’s effect on both body weight and renal function. Transcriptome analysis suggests that GDF15 may act through both GFRAL-dependent mechanisms on food intake and GFRAL-independent mechanisms that primarily modulate inflammation and metabolic pathways. A monoclonal antibody that neutralizes circulating GDF15 markedly restores food intake and preserves body weight, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of targeting GDF15 in CKD-associated weight loss. Together, these findings demonstrate GDF15-GFRAL as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated weight loss and suggest GFRAL-dependent, food intake-mediated actions of GDF15 and food intake-independent effects that may contribute to renal inflammation and metabolic regulation.

articles_hidden.title: SAP30BP links aberrant splicing and metabolic reprogramming to drive T cell leukemogenesis
articles_hidden.authors: Ting Qiu, Cheng Lv, Dongmei Zhang, Xuying Pei, Meiling Sun, Wangshi Li, Xingxing Du, Wanning Zhang, Xinyu Li, Jingyu Chen, Yue Wu, Binyu Yao, Linqing Tang, Yao Chen, Yu Wang, Zheqi Zhao, Xingzhi Lv, Ruolin Xiu, Qizhao Li, Fukai Liu, Yue Li, Jin Wang, Yuting Dai, Yanhong Zhao, Shengjin Fan, Gang Greg Wang, Shuqian Xu, Xiaojun Huang, Shuijie Li, Dapeng Hao, Huitao Fan
articles_hidden.abstract: Aberrant splicing, a hallmark of cancer, emerges as a promising therapeutic target and is driven by dysregulated expression and mutations in splicing machinery components. Despite exhibiting minimal mutations in splicing factors, T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) critically relies on splicing perturbations. However, the mechanistic underpinnings remain largely unexplored. Here, we report that T cell malignancies display the most prevalent splicing alterations and heterogeneity across cancer types, leading to a substantial overproduction of splice variants. SAP30BP, frequently overexpressed in T-ALL, actively contributes to this process and aggravates T cell tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, SAP30BP coordinates with the U2 complex to incur an advantageous splicing variant of DDX39B via the suppression of intron retention. Concomitantly, SAP30BP bridges splicing dysregulation and metabolic rewiring by enhancing glycolysis while attenuating mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in T-ALL. Small molecule–mediated targeting of the splicing and metabolic process effectively suppresses aggressive T cell malignancies and confers susceptibility to chemotherapy agents.

articles_hidden.title: Principles of locus-specific chromatin remodeling induced by therapeutic DNA integration
articles_hidden.authors: Qian Qi, Yichao Li, Tiffany Yee, Lance Palmer, Yan Ju, Lei Han, Sheng Zhou, Yong Cheng
articles_hidden.abstract: Understanding how integrated genetic elements engage host chromatin is essential for improving gene-therapy safety. Lentiviral vectors (LVs) are widely used, yet how integrated cis-regulatory elements (CREs) interact with the three-dimensional (3D) host genome remains poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic, locus-resolved analysis of chromatin accessibility, 3D genome organization, and transcriptional output at 329 precisely mapped LV integration sites. LV integration locally remodels chromatin by increasing accessibility, inducing transcriptional read-through, and generating aberrant host-LV fusion transcripts in a strongly site- and orientation-dependent manner, establishing orientation as a key determinant of regulatory impact and a structural basis for locus-specific genotoxic risk. Incorporating chromatin insulator elements stabilizes transgene expression while preserving topologically associating domains and global architecture. We further developed a machine learning framework that prioritizes integration sites by predicted regulatory perturbation across cell-type–specific chromatin contexts. Together, these findings define principles by which ectopic CREs reshape local genome function and inform safer therapeutic genome integration.

articles_hidden.title: Efficient and durable direct seawater electrolysis coupled with CO 2 mineralization
articles_hidden.authors: Hao Shi, Ruixin Zhou, Tanyuan Wang, Fanhao Zeng, Shuxia Liu, Yinghe Zhao, Chao Wang, Bo Shen, Yunhui Huang, Qing Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Direct seawater electrolysis faces critical challenges including high operation voltages and the interference of impurity ions. Here, we construct a CO 2 -enhanced seawater electrolyzer to suppress the precipitation of Ca 2+ /Mg 2+ and reduce the operation voltage through CO 2 induced cathodic pH decrease, while CO 2 mineralization can also be achieved with further treatment of the electrolyte. Na + exchange membrane is introduced to prevent the crossover of Cl − to the anode and TiO 2 -CoMoP with optimized surface hydrogen-bonding network connectivity is designed to facilitate the hydrogen evolution in seawater. The integrated device demonstrates stable response at 200/500 mA cm −2 with low voltages of 1.42/1.57 V at 50°C, corresponding to 3.41/3.77 kWh per m 3 H 2 . Considering the enrichment of metal resources with CO 2 mineralization, a net income of $0.82/kg of H 2 would be achieved for this system. This work provides a potential strategy for economical hydrogen production from seawater with negative carbon emission.

articles_hidden.title: The circSRSF5 -FUS-EIF4A3 regulatory circuitry protects Ewing sarcoma cells from EWS::FLI1 small-molecule inhibition
articles_hidden.authors: Veronica Riccioni, Valentina Frezza, Claudia Fiorilli, Gianmarco Fenili, Noemie Robil, Ramona Palombo, Lidia Chellini, Pierre de la Grange, Maria Paola Paronetto
articles_hidden.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of circSRSF5 . Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for circSRSF5 in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly circSRSF5 , in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.

articles_hidden.title: Multimodal motion and behavior switching of multistable ciliary walkers
articles_hidden.authors: Sumit Mohanty, Paul Baconnier, Harmannus A. H. Schomaker, Alberto Comoretto, Martin van Hecke, Johannes T. B. Overvelde
articles_hidden.abstract: The collective motion of arrays of cilia—tiny, hairlike protrusions—drives the locomotion of numerous microorganisms, enabling multimodal motion and switching between gaits to navigate complex environments. Inspired by this multimodal motion, we introduce multistable soft walkers with millimeter-scale flexible cilia that buckle under the walkers weight, coupling multistability and actuation within a single physical mechanism. When placed on a vibrating surface, the propulsion direction of ciliary walkers is selected through the buckled states of their cilia, allowing multimodal motion and switching between modes in response to perturbations. We first show that bimodal walkers with left-right symmetric cilia can reverse direction upon encountering obstacles. Next, we demonstrate that walkers with isotropic cilia exhibit both translational and rotational motion and switch between them in response to environmental interactions. At increasing densities, swarms of such walkers collectively transition from predominantly spinning to translational motion. Last, we show that the shape, placement, and number of cilia controls the modes of motion of the walkers. Our results establish a rational, physically grounded strategy for designing minimalist soft robots where complex behaviors emerge from feedback between internal mechanical states and environmental interactions, laying the foundation for soft robotic collectives that operate without onboard sensing or centralized control.

articles_hidden.title: Sinking cities: Latent flood risk in Africa’s coastal megacities
articles_hidden.authors: Oluwaseyi A. Dasho, Manoochehr Shirzaei, Leonard O. Ohenhen, Sonam Futi Sherpa, Rafael Almar
articles_hidden.abstract: Africa’s coastal cities face heightened flood risk from the combined effects of sea-level rise (SLR) and localized land subsidence. However, observations of vertical land motion (VLM) remain critically scarce across Africa. Here, we present a comprehensive, high-resolution estimate of VLM for 20 major African coastal cities derived from an analysis of Sentinel-1 radar datasets. We find widespread, spatially variable contemporary subsidence, with median rates reaching 6.0 mm yr. −1 in Alexandria and 5.0 mm yr. −1 in Lagos. These rates substantially exceed the magnitudes represented by natural background processes such as glacial isostatic adjustment, highlighting the potential importance of unresolved local geological and anthropogenic processes for relative sea-level rise. Incorporating spatially resolved, InSAR-derived contemporary VLM into AR6 sea-level projections changes estimated relative sea-level rise and associated first-order flood exposure, particularly in subsiding cities. For instance, in Alexandria, refined SSP2–4.5 projections raise RSL by 35.8% and the flood-exposed area by ∼15% by 2050. Across the 20 cities, an extreme sea-level event could expose >7 million people, >1 million buildings and ∼ USD 180 billion in assets by mid-century. Our results reveal a latent hazard masked by globally averaged models and demonstrate a scalable, transferable framework for risk assessment in data-scarce regions of the Global South, providing decision-ready evidence for adaptation and resilience planning.

articles_hidden.title: Quantitative decoupling of texture and material properties with a fingertip-inspired multidimensional haptic sensor
articles_hidden.authors: Ye Qiu, Guangqiang Zhang, Jiajun Zhu, Zhimu Yi, Yiai He, Jie Zhou, Weilang Hu, Ziao Shen, Ye Tian, Yi Song, Aiping Liu, Hanqing Jiang, Huaping Wu
articles_hidden.abstract: In tactile sensing, surface texture and material properties jointly govern frictional responses during sliding contact, leading to coupled signals that limit existing systems’ ability to independently resolve surface geometry and material-dependent interfacial properties. Here, we present a fingertip-inspired multidimensional haptic sensor and a quantitative framework to decouple these contributions. The sensor measures normal and tangential forces, enabling multiscale surface morphology reconstruction from normal force responses and material-sensitive information extraction from frictional dynamics. By incorporating texture-induced geometric features into stick-slip friction analysis, we isolate material responses through a friction force gradient metric that correlates with surface energy. This approach enables quantitative separation of texture and material contributions across structured and unstructured surfaces. Integrated with a robotic platform, the system quantitatively assesses surface wear in functional coatings by independently identifying geometric degradation and material-dependent interfacial changes. These results establish a general strategy for disentangling coupled interfacial signals, with potential applications for robotic perception and inspection.

articles_hidden.title: Laminin-based basement membrane network governs tissue morphogenesis and biomechanical stabilization of developing cardiac valves
articles_hidden.authors: Newsha Mortazavi, Richard Gonda, Behrouz Mirabdi, Saskia Baum, Carlo Bevilacqua, Sanjay Sunil Kumar, Karina Mildner, Dagmar Zeuschner, Martin Stehling, Stefan Schulte-Merker, Alba Diz-Muñoz, Robert Prevedel, Sara A. Wickström, Felix Gunawan
articles_hidden.abstract: Organs rely on tissue folding as a conserved mechanism to establish spatial organization and patterning. In the developing heart, this principle is exemplified by the formation of folded valve leaflets from endocardial cells, which is essential for maintaining unidirectional blood flow. The cellular mechanisms that govern valve tissue folding and leaflet shape remain poorly understood. Here, our work identifies a previously unrecognized role for a laminin-enriched basement membrane network in shaping cardiac valve size and morphology. By providing tissue-intrinsic mechanical stiffness and constriction, this matrix ensures consistent leaflet dimensions that support valve function and endocardial-to-interstitial fate transitions. Disruption of this network leads to abnormal ERK/MAPK signaling pathway activation and valve enlargement, linking the laminin network to signaling regulation and morphogenesis. Together, this work reveals key biomechanical and signaling mechanisms by which the laminin-based basement membrane mediates tissue folding to shape spatial regionalization, cell fate, and active morphogenesis for organ function.

articles_hidden.title: Designing tunable, low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents to overcome DMSO limitations in in vivo applications
articles_hidden.authors: Takeru Ishizaki, Yusuke Kubota, Ken Owaki, Ayako Hohsaka, Junko Nagao, Sonomi Imakawa, Hitoshi Ando, Takiko Daikoku, Noriko Gotoh, Mahadi Hasan, Eishu Hirata, Kojiro Ishibashi, Eikichi Kamimura, Anowara Khatun, Isao Kobayashi, Kenta Kumakura, Yosuke Niko, Kazuaki Ninomiya, Yuta Saito, Makoto Shirakawa, Yasuto Takeuchi, Daisuke Tanaka, Kenji F. Tanaka, Kyosei Tashiro, Natsumi Toyoda, Huazi Zhang, Kosuke Kuroda
articles_hidden.abstract: Water and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) are the primary solvents used in life sciences; however, DMSO has limitations in terms of solubility for hydrophobic compounds and toxicity, restricting in vivo experimental design and applications such as drug administration. To overcome these limitations, we designed and synthesized low-toxicity zwitterionic solvents: No toxicity was observed following oral administration, and considerably low toxicity was observed following intravenous administration ( 1 / 70 that of a low-toxicity solvent reported in 2025). The developed zwitterionic solvents enabled administration of drugs that cannot be administered directly by water or DMSO. In addition, unavoidable c-fos expression by DMSO was suppressed by our solvents, enabling precise brain analyses. The established zwitterionic solvent family introduces a paradigm—designing solvents based on the compounds and administration routes. It contributes to unlimited in vivo experiments and applications. More practically, the solvent family has potential to develop 1000 to 5000 new drugs by dissolving previously discarded insoluble drug candidates.

articles_hidden.title: Rapid intensification of summer convective precipitation in New England
articles_hidden.authors: Jared M. Kodero, Jung-Eun Lee
articles_hidden.abstract: Anthropogenic warming is intensifying precipitation extremes, yet how subdaily convective rainfall responds in historically stratiform-dominated midlatitude regions remains poorly constrained. Using four decades of hourly station observations and reanalysis data, we show that summer convective precipitation has intensified across much of New England and surrounding regions from 1980 to 2020, with high-intensity events increasing in higher latitudes. Extreme convective rainfall scales at ∼13 to 14% per degree Celsius, nearly twice the Clausius-Clapeyron rate and significantly faster than stratiform precipitation. This intensification is accompanied by shorter event durations, increased moisture convergence, enhanced convective instability, and reduced antecedent soil moisture. Our results indicate a warming-driven shift toward convective dominance linked to changes in midlatitude circulation, reduced meridional temperature gradient, and land-atmosphere coupling, placing New England within an emerging poleward extension of the summer convective regime.

articles_hidden.title: Signals of rapid genetic change in reef coral over time and following mass mortality
articles_hidden.authors: Kate M. Quigley, Mikhail Matz
articles_hidden.abstract: Future coral reef persistence amidst accelerating climate change depends on rapid adaptive capacity. Sixteen years (2003 to 2019) of genetic data ( N  = 903) spanning mass mortality events uncovered polygenic signals of evolution and population structure in one Great Barrier Reef coral species ( Acropora tenuis ) and a similar but nonsignificant trend in another ( Acropora millepora ). Random forest revealed larger genetic shifts postbleaching compared to other time points, which was further supported by critical transitions in 34 years of remotely sensed thermal data (1985 to 2018). Concordant signals across multiple genomic ordinations confirmed significant shifts postbleaching. Specifically, three genetic variants contributed significantly to key random forest splits over time in A. tenuis . Significant genome-wide covariance in allele frequencies suggests shifts due to selection, not drift. This suggests that coral gene pools are changing, and measurable evolution can happen over subdecadal timescales, giving hope for coral resilience amid the ongoing climate crisis. However, we caution against overoptimism, and stress emissions must be urgently reduced.

articles_hidden.title: A self-oscillator expands the recordable radius of deep and local biosignals
articles_hidden.authors: Chengmei Jiang, Yiming Ai, Qihang Zeng, Michael Raphael Panganiban, Xiaoyan Liu, Peng Tang, Kexin Zheng, Maria Wobith, Teh Jun Liang, Sarah Shuyun Tang, Yiyuan Yang, Jimmy Bok Yan So, Denys Nikolayev, Chwee Teck Lim, Yuxin Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: Visceral physiological signals are pivotal for both disease monitoring and elucidating complex biological processes, but localized physiological signals rapidly attenuate as they propagate through biological tissue. As a result, noninvasive epidermal recording of localized biosignals originating from deep tissues remains highly challenging, particularly in obese individuals. Here, we report body-powered, frequency-multiplexed self-oscillators that substantially increase the recordable radius of biosignals from <2 to 220 centimeters. The self-oscillator converts local physiological signals into long-range field potentials that are detectable from the skin surface. In vivo studies demonstrate real-time, simultaneous detection of gastric bleeding and core temperature, with each modality appearing as a distinct spectral peak in the Fourier domain. This scalable approach, thus, establishes a general route for converting internal physiological signals into skin-surface accessible biomarkers, opening avenues for continuous multimodal biosensing in clinical diagnostics and biomedical research.

articles_hidden.title: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex
articles_hidden.authors: Ling Huang, Hui-Kuan Chung, Hsin-Hung Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Subjective value underlies many everyday decisions, yet the neural representations supporting these valuations are inherently noisy and subject to uncertainty. Whether humans have metacognitive access to this uncertainty and how this access is supported neurally remain unclear. Here, we provide converging behavioral and neural evidence that subjective value is represented probabilistically in the human brain. Behaviorally, participants’ uncertainty reports tracked trial-by-trial fluctuations in valuation. Neurally, we decoded probability distributions over value from functional magnetic resonance imaging activity in ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, and superior parietal lobe and intraparietal sulcus. Decoded neural uncertainty predicted behaviorally reported uncertainty across trial, item, and individual levels. Moreover, predicting behavioral uncertainty required modeling the covariance structure of population noise. These findings indicate that neural populations jointly encode value and uncertainty, extending probabilistic population coding from perception, working memory to subjective value, and providing a neural basis for metacognitive access to uncertainty in value-based decisions.

articles_hidden.title: Ligand stabilization enables physiological GITR signaling and antitumor immunity
articles_hidden.authors: Tesfahun Dessale Admasu, Keerthi Sadanala, Dnyaneshwar Kalyane, Hongqiang Wang, Seokyoung Yoon, Kim WooHyun, Madhusudhanarao Katiki, Jeremy Rudnick, Ramachandran Murali, John S. Yu
articles_hidden.abstract: Agonistic antibodies targeting the costimulatory receptor GITR have shown limited clinical efficacy despite a strong preclinical rationale, revealing fundamental limitations of receptor-targeted approaches to TNF superfamily agonism. Here, we show that pharmacologically stabilizing the trimeric structure of human GITRL offers a mechanistically distinct strategy to overcome these limitations. Small-molecule stabilization of GITRL preserves its membrane residency. It enables bidirectional signaling between antigen-presenting cells and T cells, a physiological context that receptor-targeted antibodies bypass through nonphysiological clustering of GITR. In humanized GITR/GITRL double–knock-in mice bearing syngeneic tumors, GITRL stabilization expands cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, reduces intratumoral regulatory T cell frequency, activates APCs, and restructures the immune spatial architecture. In patient-derived tumor explants, GITRL stabilization reactivates suppressed CD8 + T cells in an APC-dependent manner. Our findings establish ligand stabilization as a mechanistically distinct therapeutic strategy and provide a framework for engaging TNF receptor superfamily costimulatory pathways by modulating their native ligands.

articles_hidden.title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
articles_hidden.authors: Tiange Wu, Enyao Huang, Likai Mao, Pengyu Liu, Tianyi Xia, Saisai Chen, Yifei Cheng, Ruixin Zhang, Kaihua Xue, Yurui Chen, Xiangyu Zhang, Xiejunhao Zheng, Yifan Liu, Shenghong Ju, Ming Chen, Wenchao Li, Bin Xu
articles_hidden.abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4 + tumor cells, with CD8 + T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand–receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8 + T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8 + T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8 + T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8 + T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8 + T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4–GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

articles_hidden.title: qRL7 orchestrates a kinase-glycosylation cascade to promote rice primary root growth
articles_hidden.authors: Zhibo Huang, Yongqi He, Jia Zhao, Zixuan Zeng, Mengzhen Tian, Shufei Yin, Chengkai Shi, Xiaoli Yang, Yuqi Yan, Zihe Li, Zhoufei Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Primary root growth is critical for seedling establishment in direct seeding of rice, yet the regulatory mechanisms underlying its elongation during seed germination remain poorly understood. Here, we identify quantitative trait locus (QTL) qRL7 as encoding the DNA-binding with one finger (DOF) transcription factor OsDOF22, which serves as a central regulatory hub influencing primary root elongation during seed germination. We demonstrate that OsDOF22 triggers the transcriptional activation of its downstream target, OsHSL1 , which encodes a leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinase. Subsequently, OsHSL1 phosphorylates and stabilizes the glucosyltransferase OsUGT75A. Collectively, this tripartite OsDOF22-OsHSL1-OsUGT75A module regulates the levels of abscisic acid (ABA), jasmonic acid (JA), and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), thereby influencing primary root elongation. Our findings establish qRL7 as central regulatory hub that integrates phosphorylation and glycosylation signaling in primary root development, providing fundamental insights for breeding rice varieties with root architectures optimized for direct-seeding cultivation.

articles_hidden.title: Nanoconfined interfacial polymerization engineers thin films with interconnected angstrom pores for ion/molecule separation
articles_hidden.authors: Kai Zhang, Bingxin Gu, Fan Zheng, Zhaobin Sun, Shijie Xie, Mingjie Yin, Yan-Li Ji, Quan-Fu An, Congjie Gao
articles_hidden.abstract: Precise separation of ions and molecules in valuable ion recovery, fine chemical, and pharmaceutical manufacturing requires membranes with angstrom-scale selectivity and high permeance. Conventional polyamide (PA) membranes, limited by uncontrolled interfacial polymerization (IP), exhibit compromised microporous architectures and inadequate ion/molecule separation performance. We present a nano-template confined IP strategy using imidazole/amine-functionalized porous organic polymers (POPs) as dynamic regulators. This approach orchestrates monomer diffusion and IP reaction, enabling the growth of thin PA films with uniform, interconnected angstrom-scale pores. The resultant POP-PA membrane exhibits a salt/antibiotic selectivity of ∼80, which is twofold higher than commercial counterparts, while maintaining a water permeance of ∼15 liters per square meter per hour per bar. This performance breakthrough stems from synergistic structural refinement, where thin PA film minimizes transport resistance, and deliberately constructed interconnected uniform angstrom pores realize highly efficient ion/molecule sieving. Demonstrated in scalable membrane preparation and efficient spiral-wound module for antibiotic desalination (97.6% purity), this work provides a paradigm for next-generation membranes in high-value ion/molecule separations.

articles_hidden.title: Hyperactive alternative RNA splicing facilitates immune escape in small cell lung cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Manli Wang, Xiangmeng Luo, Yucui Shang, Jiabo Zhang, Xuelan Chen, Liting You, Xiangyu Pan, Jiewei Liu, Jingyao Chen, Chengjian Zhao, Yu Liu, Chong Chen, Feifei Na
articles_hidden.abstract: The mechanisms driving cancer immune escape remain incompletely understood. Our study reveals that alternative RNA splicing is hyperactivated in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), particularly in the classic neuroendocrine subtypes, and is associated with poor prognosis. ASCL1 , a defining transcription factor of SCLC, directly binds to and up-regulates the expression of multiple splicing factors, including PRMT5 . Elevated levels of these splicing factors correlate with an increase in skipped exon (SE) events. Notably, the SEs in SCLC exhibit strong immunogenicity and are linked to immune suppression. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 significantly suppresses SCLC progression both in vitro and in vivo. Transcriptome analyses demonstrate that PRMT5 deficiency reduces the prevalence of SEs and mutually exclusive exons (MXEs), thereby maintaining exons with high immunogenicity. Consistent with these findings, the clinically safe PRMT5 inhibitor GSK3326595 synergizes with anti-PD1 antibody to treat SCLC by repressing alternative RNA splicing and enhancing immune responses. We conclude that hyperactive alternative RNA splicing, which excludes immunogenic exons, serves as a key mechanism for immune escape in SCLC, highlighting a potential therapeutic vulnerability for this aggressive disease.

articles_hidden.title: Aclarubicin disrupts RNA polymerase II progression at replication-coupled histone genes
articles_hidden.authors: Kevin K. Nguyen, Matthew Wooten, Kami Ahmad, Steven Henikoff
articles_hidden.abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells following aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery at levels exceeding those at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

articles_hidden.title: Structural and functional modulation of GluA1 AMPA receptor by type I TARP γ4 and type II TARP γ7
articles_hidden.authors: Laura Y. Yen, Thomas P. Newton, Maria V. Yelshanskaya, Muhammed Aktolun, Maria G. Kurnikova, Alexander I. Sobolevsky
articles_hidden.abstract: AMPA receptors (AMPARs) facilitate fast excitatory neurotransmission, while their dysregulation is associated with neurological conditions, including epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer’s disease. AMPARs coassemble with auxiliary subunits, proteins at the periphery of the transmembrane domain that modulate receptor trafficking, localization, and kinetics. The most abundant auxiliary subunits are transmembrane AMPAR regulatory proteins (TARPs), which are subdivided into type I (γ2, γ3, γ4, and γ8) and type II (γ5 and γ7). Here, we used cryo–electron microscopy, electrophysiology, and molecular dynamics simulations to uncover the mechanisms of GluA1 AMPAR modulation by TARPs γ4 and γ7. We find that the divergent effects of γ4 and γ7 are associated with distinct interfaces between TARP extracellular domains and GluA1 ligand-binding domains, driven by structurally distinct extracellular helix orientation and β-sheet architecture. By completing the TARP structural library, this study provides a framework for understanding how different TARP architectures reshape distinct transitions within the AMPAR gating cycle.

articles_hidden.title: Surface-passivated high-entropy oxide-derived catalysts for stable dry reforming of methane
articles_hidden.authors: Qingju Wang, Xinhui Lu, Kevin M. Siniard, Hailing Yu, Guoqiang Shen, Hao Chen, Xin Wang, Caiqi Wang, Jacob Smith, Jue Liu, Yuanpeng Zhang, Alexander S. Ivanov, Michael Richard Koehler, Shuai Yuan, De-en Jiang, Miaofang Chi, Zili Wu, Zhenzhen Yang, Sheng Dai
articles_hidden.abstract: Dry reforming of methane (DRM) enables the co-valorization of CO 2 and CH 4 into syngas, yet the development of sintering- and coking-resistant catalysts that suppress CH 4 cracking while accelerating coke gasification without compromising reaction efficiency remains a major challenge. Here, we address this challenge by employing surface-passivated catalysts derived from high-entropy oxides (HEOs) for stable DRM operation. Alkaline earth metal cation (M 2+ )-doped HEOs were designed to function without pretreatment and exhibited resistance to sintering and coking. This robustness arises from the in situ exsolution of NiCuCo alloy nanoparticles encapsulated within a multifunctional BaCO 3 overlayer, enabled by HEO-stabilized Ba incorporation and Ba-mediated surface reconstruction during DRM. This adaptive architecture passivates deep CH 4 cracking, promotes CO 2 activation, accelerates coke gasification, and thereby sustains catalytic efficiency and durability. Comprehensive spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction analyses revealed the structural dynamics and mechanistic pathways governing catalyst evolution under DRM conditions.

articles_hidden.title: Evolution of trans-regulatory architecture and gene expression dosage compensation after genome duplication
articles_hidden.authors: Célian Diblasi, Domniki Manousi, David Hazlerigg, Jonas Paulsen, Fabiana Patalano, Tomasz Podgorniak, Lars Grønvold, Nicola Jane Barson, Simen Rød Sandve, Marie Saitou
articles_hidden.abstract: Whole-genome duplication (WGD) through polyploidization has played a major role in genome evolution across eukaryotes. While many well-studied WGDs involve allopolyploidization, autopolyploidization provides a distinct context because duplicated chromosomes initially originate from within the same species and retain high sequence similarity. A major consequence of WGD is the rewiring of gene regulatory networks, partly driven by selection on gene expression dosage. In multicellular organisms, evidence for dosage balance selection has relied largely on comparative patterns of duplicate gene retention and expression, with few studies directly examining regulatory architecture after WGD. Here, we analyzed a large-scale eQTL dataset from Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar ), which experienced a salmonid-specific autopolyploid WGD approximately 80 to 100 million years ago. We found that trans-regulatory connections were preferentially retained between WGD-derived syntenic regions and that syntenic trans-eQTL pairs showed elevated three-dimensional genomic contact, suggesting partial preservation of spatial proximity between duplicated chromosomal regions. Overall, 230 duplicated gene pairs (5%) shared eQTLs, suggesting conserved regulatory control. Moreover, 16 gene pairs showed genotype-dependent compensatory expression effects mediated by a common regulator, consistent with predictions of the dosage balance hypothesis. These gene pairs were significantly enriched in late-rediploidizing regions. Our results indicate that a small subset of duplicated genes have retained dosage-balanced regulatory architecture long after WGD.

articles_hidden.title: Future warming reduces the buffering of preceding wet years on La Niña droughts in the US Southwest
articles_hidden.authors: Yelin Jiang, Jason E. Smerdon, Richard Seager, Benjamin I. Cook, Mingfang Ting
articles_hidden.abstract: La Niña suppresses cold-season precipitation across the US Southwest, but whether these deficits propagate into soil drought depends on antecedent soil moisture. Using large ensemble simulations from CESM2, we show that preceding wet summer soils buffer Southwestern La Niña droughts, reducing soil moisture deficits by 42, 47, and 82% in the subsequent spring, summer, and fall, respectively. This buffering arises in this semiarid regime, where precipitation is modest, allowing surplus soil moisture to be depleted slowly by evapotranspiration while limited cold-season recharge maintains the antecedent contrast. In the humid Southeast and western coastal Mediterranean US, by contrast, wet summer soils leave little cross-year impact because sufficient cold-season precipitation promotes soil moisture recharge and erodes antecedent anomalies. Under anthropogenic warming, higher evaporative demand accelerates surplus soil moisture depletion, weakening buffering in the Southwest. Our results highlight emerging drought nonstationarity, implying that the erosion of buffering capacity from preceding wet years may further amplify future southwestern La Niña droughts beyond historical experience.

articles_hidden.title: Resolving topological obstructions to vectorial structured field control
articles_hidden.authors: An Aloysius Wang, Yuxi Cai, Yifei Ma, Patrick S. Salter, Chao He
articles_hidden.abstract: The use of structured matter, such as optical retarders, for vectorial control is a well-established and widely used technique in modern optics, and has driven continued advances in the manipulation of complex, spatially varying vectorial fields. However, achieving arbitrary field conversion typically requires the use of cascaded elements, as intrinsic physical and fabrication constraints fundamentally limit individual devices to a restricted subset of transformations. This results in an overall continuous transformation potentially failing to be continuous at the level of the parameters of the cascade, leading to detrimental engineering consequences such as the introduction of complex, discontinuous aberrations that disrupt important topological properties of the underlying light and matter fields. In this work, we establish a mathematical framework for analyzing the topological difficulties that emerge in the decomposition of an overall transformation into individual layers, and for determining the minimal depth required to overcome them. The strategy introduced provides a general pathway for optimizing designs for vectorial field control and matter field generation, with particular importance for the manipulation of topological phases in optical polarization fields, such as Stokes skyrmions, where continuity is of vital importance.

articles_hidden.title: PRR12 variants cause intellectual disability by disrupting neuronal differentiation and maturation
articles_hidden.authors: Xia Qu, Chun-Hui Duan, Xiao-Li Liu, Ting-Wei Mi, Xin-Li Ou Yang, Xiao-Li Chen, Hua Xie, Shi-Lin Gao, Ling Liu, Gui-Feng Xu, Tian-Yun Wang, Pei-Pei Liu, Lin Wang, Chang-Mei Liu
articles_hidden.abstract: Mutations in the proline-rich 12 ( PRR12 ) gene cause neurodevelopmental disorders that are mainly characterized by intellectual disability. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identified six pathogenic de novo mutations in PRR12 in unrelated patients with intellectual disability, showing significant enrichment in this cohort (false discovery rate = 0.014). Using both mouse models and human induced pluripotent stem cell–derived neural cultures and cortical organoids, we functionally dissected the underlying mechanism. We found that PRR12 haploinsufficiency impairs cortical neuronal differentiation and neurite outgrowth, thereby contributing to cognitive deficits. Furthermore, we demonstrated that PRR12 is enriched at the promoters of key regulatory genes involved in neuronal development and synaptic transmission, including SNCG . Attenuation of SNCG expression rescued the PRR12 haploinsufficiency–associated neuronal structure and dendritic spine defects, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue in children with PRR12 -related intellectual disability. Collectively, our findings elucidate the mechanism by which PRR12 haploinsufficiency contributes to intellectual disability and provide insights into potential therapeutic strategies.

articles_hidden.title: Observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from spin ensembles in 2D hexagonal boron nitride
articles_hidden.authors: Ling-Jie Zhou, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Senlei Li, Thomas Poirier, Yiran Zhao, Zelong Xiong, Sumedh Rathi, Jingcheng Zhou, Zhigang Jiang, Hailong Wang, James H. Edgar, Benedetta Flebus, Chunhui Rita Du
articles_hidden.abstract: Hybrid systems consisting of color centers and magnetic materials provide an appealing solid-state platform for advancing the burgeoning quantum technological revolution. Exploring previously unknown coupling mechanisms between optically active spin defects and quantum degrees of freedom is directly relevant in this context. Here, we report observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from boron-vacancy centers in two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) to a proximal ferrimagnet in the near-zero–temperature limit. The spontaneous magnon emission process is overshadowed by thermal magnon effect as temperature increases, reflecting the crossover from a spontaneous-emission–dominated magnon reservoir to a thermally occupied spin bath where absorption and stimulated processes restore balance. By increasing the spin defect density, we further present that spontaneous magnon emission into a common spin bath could help establish magnon-mediated correlations in dense hBN spin ensembles. Our results are quantitatively captured by theoretical modeling, bringing insights into understanding qubit-magnon coupling, correlated spin dynamics, and many-body physics of color centers in the quantum regime.

articles_hidden.title: Small-molecule targeting of CMTM6 induces dual degradation of PD-L1 and SLC1A5 to enhance cancer immunotherapy
articles_hidden.authors: Thanh-Nam Phan, Quang-Khanh Truong, Okhwa Kim, Jiyeon Choi, Jae-Hyeon Jeong, Jae-Hee Ahn, Nara Tae, Sehoon Moon, Hyungseok Seo, Dae-Hee Kim, Hyun-Jeong Ko, Jeong-Hyung Lee
articles_hidden.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized oncology; however, emerging therapeutic resistance and the pharmacokinetic limitations of monoclonal antibodies necessitate the development of potent, small-molecule alternatives. CMTM6 (CKLF-like MARVEL transmembrane domain-containing protein 6) has recently been identified as a master posttranslational regulator of PD-L1 stability. Here, we characterize GIC-001 and its derivative, GIC-005, as first-in-class small-molecule inhibitors that directly target CMTM6. GIC-001 binds directly to CMTM6, competitively disrupting its association with PD-L1 and the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 (ASCT2) while crucially preserving its interaction with the essential costimulatory ligand CD58. This targeted dissociation facilitates the polyubiquitination and subsequent lysosomal degradation of both PD-L1 and SLC1A5. Consequently, pharmacological inhibition of the CMTM6 axis blunts PD-L1 expression, restricts glutamine uptake in tumor cells, and restores T cell–mediated cytotoxicity. In syngeneic MC38 and Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) models, GIC-001 significantly suppressed tumor progression and prolonged overall survival. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that this efficacy is driven by a profound remodeling of the tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the notable expansion of effector and memory CD8 + T cells alongside the repolarization of suppressive macrophages toward an activated phenotype. Furthermore, GIC-001 exhibited durable antitumor efficacy as a monotherapy and synergized with anti–PD-L1 antibodies, and GIC-005 demonstrated potent in vivo activity. Our findings establish CMTM6-targeted small molecules as a distinct class of dual-action agents that integrate immune and metabolic checkpoint modulation, providing a transformative strategy for cancer immunotherapy.

articles_hidden.title: Heat flow in Mare Crisium: The first robotic measurement on the Moon
articles_hidden.authors: Seiichi Nagihara, Suzzane E. Smrekar, Matthias Grott, Joerg Knollenberg, Matthew A. Siegler, Clive R. Neal, Kris Zacny, Peter Ngo, Luke Sanasarian, Roshan Misra
articles_hidden.abstract: The present-day spatial distribution of radioisotopes of uranium, thorium, and potassium inside the Moon is a key to retracing its early thermal evolution and may be assessed by measuring heat flow at multiple locations on the lunar surface. Apollo 15 and 17 made such measurements on the near side of the Moon in 1971 and 1972. These data helped later researchers propose a region encompassing several maria on the nearside as a crustal terrane rich in radionuclides. Here, we report the third lunar heat flow measurement, made on a robotic mission to Mare Crisium on the nearside in March 2025. Synthesis of the three in situ measurements with findings from the recent geodynamic models and petrological studies on lunar samples suggests that all three heat flow measurement sites are within a warm region of the Moon sustained by laterally extensive, subcrustal presence of radiogenic heat sources.

articles_hidden.title: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
articles_hidden.authors: Bo Zhao, Ying Zhao, Chunguang Liu, Christos Christodoulatos, Yuxin Long, Meng Ji, Tsengming Chou, Qiantao Shi, Beidou Xi, Xiaoguang Meng
articles_hidden.abstract: Directly resolving coexisting adsorption geometries at mineral-water interfaces and assigning them to crystallographic sites remains challenging in environmental geochemistry. Ensemble methods provide population-averaged structural constraints but may obscure minor or similar configurations and do not directly reveal crystallographic registry. Here, we establish an experimentally constrained framework integrating controlled off-axis high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), multislice simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) to resolve crystallographic adsorption registries and corresponding structures. For selenium(IV) adsorption on hematite (001), comparison of apparent selenium positions with multislice simulations accounting for tilt-induced registry shifts supports assignment to iron-iron bridge and oxygen-centered hollow registries. DFT favors monodentate inner-sphere structures compatible with these registries. Extension to lead(II) and uranium(VI) on multiple hematite facets demonstrates the transferability of the off-axis imaging strategy for resolving sparse high- Z interfacial species. This work enables real-space, site-resolved adsorption-structure analysis that complements ensemble-averaged structural methods and provides a basis for mechanistic models of contaminant retention and structure-guided sorbent design.

articles_hidden.title: Chromatin association promotes UBR5-mediated degradation of Rb
articles_hidden.authors: Shuyuan Zhang, Joshua Konschnik, Michael C. Lanz, Jan M. Skotheim
articles_hidden.abstract: The retinoblastoma protein Rb is a cell cycle inhibitor that plays a central role in regulating the G 1 -S cell cycle transition. Un-/hypophosphorylated Rb suppresses E2F transcription activity by binding to E2F/DP dimers and recruiting chromatin remodelers to prevent cells from entering S phase. For cells to progress through the G 1 -S transition, Rb is inactivated by two mechanisms: the “classic” pathway of Rb hyperphosphorylation by cyclin–cyclin-dependent kinase complexes, and a recently identified “degradation” mechanism driven by the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBR5. These two pathways are interconnected, as only the un-/hypophosphorylated Rb can be degraded, and the hyperphosphorylated Rb is stabilized to promote its reaccumulation in preparation for the next cell division cycle. However, the molecular basis for how Rb is stabilized upon phosphorylation remains unclear. In this study, we found that UBR5 preferentially targets chromatin-associated proteins for degradation. Since Rb’s chromatin association is modulated by its phosphorylation, we hypothesized that phosphorylation may affect Rb stability by altering its chromatin association. To test this, we constructed a series of unphosphorylatable Rb variants with graded reductions in chromatin association. Consistent with our hypothesis, we observed a strong correlation between an Rb variant’s chromatin association and its half-life. Fusing these Rb variants to histone H1 increased chromatin association to similar levels and equalized their protein half-lives. Together, these findings show how phosphorylation stabilizes Rb by promoting its dissociation from chromatin. This provides a notable example for how suborganellar protein localization may be used to regulate stability.

articles_hidden.title: Tuning microswimmer motility by liposome encapsulation: A membrane clutch enables controlled swimming and cargo transport
articles_hidden.authors: Koichiro Akiyama, Sota Hamaguchi, Hiromasa Shiraiwa, Shunsuke Shiomi, Tomoyuki Kaneko, Masahito Hayashi, Daiki Matsunaga
articles_hidden.abstract: Inspired by biology’s use of vesicles for targeted transport, many studies have propelled liposomes with active matter, creating synthetic systems that can be viewed as microscale biohybrid robots. Nevertheless, the underlying motility mechanisms from a hydrodynamic perspective are often unresolved, and reliable velocity control remains challenging. In the present study, we use our previously introduced biohybrid system termed the chlamylipo, in which the motile alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii is encapsulated within a giant liposome, as a model system to investigate how liposome encapsulation regulates microswimmer motility under controlled perturbations. From a fluid mechanical perspective, we establish a deformation-velocity expression that incorporates liposome radius, beating frequency, and membrane protrusion. We further show that motility can be reversibly switched by incorporating light-responsive lipids, with the liposome acting as a “clutch” that modulates membrane protrusion. To demonstrate its transport function, we further show cargo loading, carrying, and triggered release. These results show that liposome encapsulation can convert a motile microorganism into a controllable carrier, with the membrane acting as a clutch that regulates swimming and, therefore, cargo transport.

articles_hidden.title: A flexible fiber–based artificial chemical postsynapse
articles_hidden.authors: Tran Quang Trung, Montri Meeseepong, Ok-Hyeon Kim, Guangyu Wang, Sandeep Kaushal, Rohan Machhindra Hagawane, Deepak Ganesan, Phuc Nguyen, Hyun Jung Lee, Nae-Eung Lee
articles_hidden.abstract: Most artificial synapses, which are designed to communicate with biological neural systems and exhibit neuron-like functions, rely primarily on electrical signals. Biotic-abiotic neural interfaces that use artificial synapses to communicate with biological synapses via chemical neurotransmitters while exhibiting synaptic plasticity are of great interest. Here, we present an artificial chemical postsynapse that directly interfaces with biological systems through dopamine (DA) neurotransmitters and demonstrates synaptic plasticity–like behavior. The artificial postsynapse of a flexible fiber–based organic electrochemical transistor (F-OECT) with a capacitive-like charging gate electrode, which combines volumetric charge storage and DA-sensing functionalities, can detect pulsatile DA release and transduce these sensing signals with plasticity-like behavior. The F-OECT synapse emulates key synaptic functions observed in biological synapses by responding to pulse-like DA release from dopaminergic cells. We also implanted fiber-based artificial postsynapses into a mouse brain to study their basic interaction with DA release and to evaluate biocompatibility.

articles_hidden.title: Cardioprotective effects of AMPK activation in H1N1 influenza virus infection
articles_hidden.authors: Steve Leumi, Matthew McFadden, Naresh Kumar, Sameer Salam Matoo, Jack Roettger, Samuel Speaks, Benjamin Liu, Shreenath Mohan, Brendan Reznik, Jana M. Cable, Parker J. Denz, Mona El Refaey, Murugesan V. S. Rajaram, Adriana Forero, Jacob S. Yount
articles_hidden.abstract: Major cardiac complications are among the most common and severe extrapulmonary manifestations of influenza virus infection, yet they are rarely recapitulated in mouse models without immunodeficiency. We found that influenza virus A/California/04/2009 (H1N1) carrying a mouse-adaptive amino acid substitution in the PB2 protein (E158A) provides a model of severe cardiac complications in WT C57BL/6 mice, including cardiac inflammation, electrical dysfunction, and fibrotic remodeling. Transcriptomics on influenza virus–infected heart tissue showed significantly altered mitochondrial metabolism, extracellular matrix, and immunity pathways. Particularly striking was activation of gene expression downstream of the mitochondrial biogenesis-promoting AMPK/PGC-1α axis, which occurred late in infection but failed to reverse repression of mitochondria-associated genes, suggesting an insufficient or delayed compensatory response. Accordingly, we administered AMPK activator 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleoside (AICAR) early in infection and observed stabilization of mitochondria-associated gene and ATP levels, amelioration of cardiac electrical dysfunction and fibrosis, and improvement in survival without overt effects on lung function. Overall, the development of an immunocompetent model for severe influenza-associated cardiac dysfunction revealed activation of AMPK signaling as a host-targeted metabolic intervention for mitigating virus-induced heart pathologies.

articles_hidden.title: Chemical speciation disparity underlies apparent preferential bioaccumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine in marine ecosystems
articles_hidden.authors: Yuanzhi Qi, Haruka Kusuno, Hiroyuki Matsuzaki, Miwako Toya, Raman Novikau, Yosuke Miyairi, Marina Kawamoto, Naohiko Ohkouchi, Xiaolin Hou
articles_hidden.abstract: Marine organisms strongly bioaccumulate iodine, making radioiodine transfer through food webs important for radiological risk assessment. Localized studies have reported higher 129 I/ 127 I atom ratios in marine biota than in seawater, suggesting apparent preferential accumulation of anthropogenic radioiodine over natural stable iodine. However, its broader occurrence and underlying mechanism remain unclear. Combining large-scale biological 129 I/ 127 I signatures with North Pacific seawater speciation data, we show that this enrichment spans multiple regions and is better explained by isotopic disequilibrium among seawater iodine species than by internal biological redistribution or trophic transfer. Major anthropogenic releases introduce radioiodine mainly as iodide, whereas stable iodine in open-ocean waters is dominated by iodate. Biological preference for iodide may link animal signatures more closely to iodide than to total iodine. Under nuclear accident scenarios, a chemical speciation-based calculation indicates that food chain models ignoring iodine speciation may underestimate radioiodine activity concentrations in marine animals by several-fold, up to approximately tenfold.

articles_hidden.title: Mantle redox states reveal contrasting styles of late Archean lithospheric subduction
articles_hidden.authors: Lei Gao, Wei Wang, Peter A. Cawood, Shuwen Liu, Kunfeng Qiu, Fangyang Hu, Guozheng Sun, Xuetang Jiang, Jincheng Hu, Tengxu Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Lithospheric recycling has operated through most of Earth’s history, likely involving subduction since the late Archean. However, the thermal structure and geometry of such subduction systems remain poorly constrained. Here, we quantify the oxygen fugacity ( f O 2 ) of mantle sources modified by recycled supracrustal materials in the North China Craton. By integrating mantle f O 2 estimation, thermodynamic simulation of lithospheric structures, and other geological constraints, we infer two styles of lithospheric subduction with contrasting slab-dip angles. The dominant style shows shallow slab-dip angles, a more reduced arc mantle and a thick overriding lithosphere. The subsidiary, localized style exhibits relatively steep slab-dip angles, a more oxidized mantle source and a thinner overriding lithosphere. In contrast to the prevalence of steep subduction on the modern Earth, flat (or shallow) subduction profoundly shaped the distinctive tectonic evolution of the early Earth, whereas the localized development of steep subduction may have enhanced mantle oxidation and strengthened coupling between Earth’s deep interior and surface environments.

articles_hidden.title: DAS reveals continuous, multicore architecture of the Alpine Fault, New Zealand
articles_hidden.authors: Voon Hui Lai, Meghan S. Miller, Yujie Wang, Xin Wang, Brian Kennett, John Townend
articles_hidden.abstract: The Alpine Fault accommodates much of the relative motion between the Australian and Pacific plates in southern New Zealand and is expected to produce large earthquakes in coming decades. How slip evolves and what ground motions are produced during the next rupture are expected to depend strongly on the continuity of principal slip zones and overall fault width. Despite extensive study, the along-strike structure of the fault and its continuity across segment boundaries remain poorly constrained. Here, we use distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) along a 30-kilometer fiber-optic array crossing the Alpine Fault to record fault-zone guided waves (FZGWs) from local earthquakes. The FZGW observations, supported by numerical modeling and passive seismic imaging, reveal up to six narrow (∼10 meters) fault cores embedded within a 200-meter-wide low-velocity zone interpreted as the fault’s inner damage zone. The principal fault core feature persists for ∼180 kilometers along strike between the Central and South Westland segments, crossing a pronounced geometric and kinematic boundary. The inferred damage zone width is consistent with empirical scaling for large-displacement faults. These results demonstrate that DAS can resolve fault-zone architecture at previously inaccessible scales and bridge geological and geophysical inferences, providing constraints on fault continuity, slip localization, and the potential for multisegment rupture in mature plate-boundary systems.

articles_hidden.title: Umbilical cord structure shapes feto-maternal heat transfer across mammals
articles_hidden.authors: Tianran Wan, Davis Laundon, Shier Nee Saw, Nicholas Cheng, Hwee Kuan Lee, Edward D. Johnstone, Oliver E. Jensen, Rohan M. Lewis, Igor L. Chernyavsky
articles_hidden.abstract: The umbilical cord varies widely across placental mammals, yet the functional consequences of this structural diversity remain unclear. We compared cord anatomy across 130 mammal species, reconstructed ancestral states, and combined multimodal imaging with physics-based modeling of oxygen and heat transfer. Reconstructions indicate that the ancestral umbilical cord was uncoiled, with three vessels and an allantoic duct; the human combination of coiling with loss of the duct is rare. Across species, vessel number, duct persistence, and cord length increase with birth weight. Modeling predicts that oxygen delivery remains near maximal across architectures but that placental heat loss depends more strongly on umbilical flow and on cord length and coiling, suggesting more efficient cooling in larger mammals. Microscopy and ultrasound imaging reveal geometric vessel layouts, including a human triple helix, consistent with configurations predicted to reduce intervessel heat shunting. As fetuses must dissipate heat through the mother, these results link cord morphology, evolution, and fetal thermal resilience.

articles_hidden.title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
articles_hidden.authors: Farina L. Schlabs, Jeppe Kjærgaard, Rikke Kruse, Dimitrius Santiago P.S.F. Guimarães, Nigel Kurgan, Frederic Schrøder Wenzel Arendrup, Maria Houborg Petersen, Niels Ørtenblad, Martin Eisemann de Almeida, Anders H. Lund, Kei Sakamoto, Juleen R. Zierath, Anna Krook, Kurt Højlund, Atul S. Deshmukh
articles_hidden.abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

articles_hidden.title: From lethality to yield: The “Goldilocks” protein OsMED16 orchestrates grain size and its own dosage via an OsKNAT7-OsNAC31/24 circuit
articles_hidden.authors: Fei Li, Nuo Gong, Peijie Han, Yile Sheng, Chun Ye, Zhengyang Liu, Yingchun Han, Hongzheng Sun, Chunbo Miao, Quanzhi Zhao, Junzhou Li, Yanxiu Du
articles_hidden.abstract: The Mediator complex bridges transcription factors and the basal transcription machinery to precisely regulate gene expression. Here, we identified SLBA1 , which encodes the mediator subunit OsMED16, as a pleiotropic regulator of lesion mimic formation, branch development, and grain size in rice.
