OsMED16 acts as a “Goldilocks” protein with a strict dosage effect: complete loss of function or excessive overexpression causes lethality, while partial dysfunction or high overexpression triggers spontaneous cell death. Only optimal expression ensures normal growth. Natural variation and genetic analyses confirmed its role in grain size control. Mechanistically, OsMED16 physically interacts with the transcription factor OsKNAT7, which differentially modulates two NAC partners, repressing the transcriptional activation activity of OsNAC31 while enhancing that of OsNAC24. Through this interaction, OsMED16 suppresses the OsKNAT7-OsNAC24 module, thereby modulating the expression of key grain-size regulators GW2 , GW5 , and D11 . Intriguingly, the OsMED16 promoter contains adjacent binding motifs for OsKNAT7 and OsNAC31. OsNAC31 serves as the primary activator of OsMED16 transcription, whereas OsKNAT7 plays a dual role by weakly activating it while antagonizing OsNAC31-mediated activation. OsNAC24 further fine-tunes OsMED16 expression via the OsKNAT7-OsNAC31 cascade. This forms an auto-regulatory feedback loop wherein OsMED16 modulates its own expression by repressing OsNAC31 through OsKNAT7-OsNAC31 module. Remarkably, field trials showed that moderate OsMED16 overexpression simultaneously enhances blast resistance and increases grain yield. This study provides insights into the dosage-dependent functions of the mediator complex and offers valuable genetic resources for the synergistic improvement of yield and resistance in rice breeding.

articles_hidden.title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
articles_hidden.authors: Wendy K. Jo, Sibylle Haid, Tabea Binger, Sebastian Brünink, Dickson Dei, Christian Drosten, Arne Kühne, Janine Müller, Samuel Oppong, Valeria Penner, Anita Wadagni, Anges Yadouleton, Thomas Pietschmann, Jan Felix Drexler
articles_hidden.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus Orthopneumovirus ) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the SH viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

articles_hidden.title: Structural basis for Ca 2+ -dependent and RyR2-selective modulation by Ryanozole
articles_hidden.authors: Yuya Otori, Takashi Murayama, Ayuna Tsutsumi, Ryosuke Ishida, Sho Takeuchi, Raymond Burton-Smith, Kazuyoshi Murata, Takashi Sakurai, Hiroyuki Kagechika, Nagomi Kurebayashi, Haruo Ogawa
articles_hidden.abstract: The cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2) is a Ca 2+ release channel essential for excitation–contraction coupling. RyR2 mutations cause severe arrhythmogenic disorders, including catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT), through gain-of-function (GOF) effects leading to aberrant Ca 2+ release. We have recently developed Ryanozole, a potential therapeutic compound for CPVT, which selectively stabilizes RyR2 in a Ca 2+ -dependent manner. Here, we define the mechanism of action of Ryanozole by combining high-resolution cryo–electron microscopy, targeted mutagenesis and functional assays. Ryanozole binds to the interface between the Ca 2+ -binding site and the pore-forming S6 helix, shifting the conformational landscape toward the closed state at low Ca 2+ . We identified key residues for Ryanozole binding and structural determinants of isoform selectivity. Notably, Ryanozole-bound RyR2 retains its ability to open at high Ca 2+ via unique conformational changes. These findings reveal the structural basis for modulation by Ryanozole and provide a framework for the development of novel RyR2-targeted therapies for CPVT.

articles_hidden.title: A spatial peroxisomal switch of AGPS drives ether lipid–induced ferroptosis in vascular calcification
articles_hidden.authors: Qing Li, Calin Zhang, Yuan Liu, Hui Li, Quanji Wang, Qian Jiang, Zihan Wang, Yanan Wang, Jin Li, Gang Xu, Fan He
articles_hidden.abstract: Vascular calcification is a life-threatening complication of chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet the metabolic changes that cause blood vessels to harden remain unclear. We found that the pathologically enhanced relocation of a lipid-producing enzyme, alkylglycerone phosphate synthase (AGPS), into cellular compartments called peroxisomes acts as a critical driver of this disease. This spatial shift, triggered by the protein PKCη (protein kinase C η), causes a surge in specific lipids that promote cell death and mineral buildup in the vessels. To disrupt this destructive process, we used generative artificial intelligence (AI) to design a custom peptide that blocks the interaction between AGPS and PKCη. When delivered systemically using lipid nanoparticles, this AI-designed therapeutic successfully prevented the enzyme’s excessive relocation, stopped toxic lipid accumulation, and profoundly reduced aortic calcification in CKD mice. Our findings uncover a crucial metabolic trigger for vascular calcification and highlight AI-guided nanotherapeutics as a promising strategy for treating vascular diseases.

articles_hidden.title: Hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on off-diagonal Peltier and Ettingshausen effects in a junction-less single material
articles_hidden.authors: Atsushi Takahagi, Yosuke Goto, Masayuki Murata, Hosei Nagano, Ken-ichi Uchida
articles_hidden.abstract: Transverse thermoelectric conversion, which interconverts heat and charge currents in orthogonal directions, is gaining attention as a driving principle for next-generation thermal management devices that do not require dissimilar material junctions or complex module structures. Transverse thermoelectric conversion is driven by various principles stemming from the breaking of structural symmetry or time-reversal symmetry, and substantial performance improvements are anticipated by simultaneously utilizing multiple principles. This study demonstrates hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on multiple phenomena within a junction-less single material. Using an active thermoelectric imaging technique based on lock-in thermography, the charge-to-heat current conversion characteristics in Mg 3 Bi 2 crystals showing anisotropic transport properties were visualized and evaluated. We successfully separated the contributions of the off-diagonal Peltier effect due to the electronic structural symmetry breaking and the ordinary Ettingshausen effect due to the time-reversal symmetry breaking under a magnetic field. These contributions operate additively within the same material, leading to the notable enhancement of the transverse thermoelectric conversion performance.

articles_hidden.title: Community and metabolic cues gate arsenate uptake via a promiscuous glycerol-3-phosphate transporter
articles_hidden.authors: Emilio Bueno, Diego Rey, Laura Alvarez, Erik Björn, Andre Mateus, Felipe Cava
articles_hidden.abstract: Arsenic is a pervasive environmental toxin that threatens all forms of life. Although phosphate transporters account for most arsenate entry in bacteria, the regulatory mechanisms that tune additional uptake routes remain poorly understood. Here we identify a regulatory circuit in Vibrio cholerae that enhances arsenate resilience by modulating expression of the glycerol-3-phosphate transporter GlpT. A screen for arsenate tolerance revealed the quorum-sensing regulators LuxO and RpoN as determinants of resistance. Epistasis and proteomic analyses placed HapR downstream of LuxO/RpoN and showed that quorum-sensing activation represses glpT , thereby reducing arsenate burden. GlpT expression is further constrained by catabolite repression, exposing dual metabolic and quorum-sensing control over this vulnerability. Heterologous expression of GlpT orthologs from diverse Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria increased arsenate sensitivity in V. cholerae , indicating that GlpT-mediated arsenate uptake is broadly conserved. Together, these findings show that bacteria mitigate toxin exposure by tuning promiscuous transporters, revealing a trade-off in which metabolic flexibility comes at the cost of toxin influx.

articles_hidden.title: Structural anisotropy governs mechanical response of fibrous hydrogel to multiaxial spherically symmetric deformation
articles_hidden.authors: Xiao He, Yuhang Huang, Durgesh Kavishvar, Sofia Morozova, Arun Ramachandran, Hossein Salahshoor, Sergey Panyukov, Michael Rubinstein, Eugenia Kumacheva
articles_hidden.abstract: Biological networks with preferential fiber alignment along a particular direction endow tissues with orientation-dependent mechanical properties. The mechanical response of structurally anisotropic fibrous networks to internally generated, spherically symmetric deformation is relevant to tumor expansion; however, it remains poorly understood. Here, we report the experimental results and theoretical studies of this deformation in a model hydrogel with controlled radial or lateral fiber orientation around an expanding spherical droplet. By integrating cavitation rheology with polarized optical microscopy, we found that the effective Young’s modulus of the hydrogels exhibits a strong dependence on fiber orientation, increasing with a higher degree of lateral fiber alignment and decreasing with stronger radial alignment. These findings agree with the results of the developed affine model accounting for the mechanical asymmetry of fibrous architectures. Our work provides the basis for understanding similar mechanical responses in structurally anisotropic biological matrices.

articles_hidden.title: Characterizing ocean flows with the scattering transform
articles_hidden.authors: Jack W. Skinner, Albion Lawrence, Jörn Callies
articles_hidden.abstract: Upper-ocean flows are a complex multiscale jigsaw puzzle of turbulence and waves. Characterizing these flows is essential for understanding their role in redistributing heat, carbon, and nutrients. While power spectral analysis offers a useful statistical descriptor of these flows, it cannot always distinguish between different types of motion. We show that the scattering transform (ST), a wavelet convolution method, can extract geometric information from flow fields, offering insights beyond the power spectrum. The ST distinguishes balanced dynamics, internal waves, and different flavors of geophysical turbulence—even when their power spectra are identical. Applied to sea surface height (SSH) fields from ocean models, the ST differentiates regions with distinct underlying dynamics. Our analysis offers a framework for interpreting SSH from satellite altimetry and for analyzing other spatial maps (e.g., from airborne and coastal radar). More generally, the ST is an appealing way to characterize complex fluid motion in a variety of contexts.

articles_hidden.title: Ubiquitination of USP5 by a bacterial effector inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation
articles_hidden.authors: Kelong Ma, Siyao Liu, Fan Jiang, Hongtao Liu, Rundong Shu, Jinli Ge, Zhao-qing Luo, Jiaqi Fu, Jiazhang Qiu
articles_hidden.abstract: The intracellular pathogen Legionella pneumophila employs a repertoire of effector proteins to manipulate the host ubiquitin signaling and subvert host immune responses. In this study, we reported that the L. pneumophila effector GobX (Lpg2455) functions as a ubiquitin ligase to target the host deubiquitinase USP5. Ubiquitination of USP5 by GobX inhibits its deubiquitination activity. Furthermore, this ubiquitination enhances the interaction between USP5 and the host E3 ligase MARCHF7, thereby facilitating MARCHF7-dependent ubiquitination of NLRP3. This modification targets NLRP3 for autophagic degradation, ultimately suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. Our findings uncover a sophisticated strategy in which a bacterial effector hijacks the host ubiquitination machinery to dampen inflammasome signaling.

articles_hidden.title: Whole-animal functional integration shaped the evolution of mammalian stance and gait
articles_hidden.authors: Peter J. Bishop, Richard W. Blob, Stephanie E. Pierce
articles_hidden.abstract: Mammalian locomotor evolution is a classic example of a major transition, characterized by a shift from sprawling to erect limb posture and extensive reorganization of synapsid postcranial anatomy. Yet, conflicting evidence has obscured how and when it unfolded. Here, we integrate paleontological and neontological datasets with computational biomechanics to illuminate synapsid locomotor transformation across 100+ million years. Using high-fidelity musculoskeletal models and physics-driven dynamic simulations, we reconstruct whole-animal gait cycles in extinct synapsids and contextualize these against extant sprawling and erect amniotes. We show that whole-animal functional coordination constrained synapsid fore- and hindlimb postures to evolve in parallel, despite asynchronous changes between anatomical modules. Further, progression toward erect locomotor mechanics was interrupted by a temporary postural reversal in the Mesozoic, facilitated by a marked decoupling between morphology and function. Only later was fully erect locomotion achieved, laying the foundation for the radiation of therian mammals into the Cenozoic.

articles_hidden.title: Selective synthesis of 1T and 2H MoS 2 via atomic spacing–tuned magnetic susceptibility
articles_hidden.authors: Yongchao Rao, Zhen Xiang, Chunhua Sun, Kai Yao, Yang Yang, Bin Yuan, Wei Lu
articles_hidden.abstract: Direct phase-selective synthesis of both phase-pure 2H and 1T Molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) remains a long-standing challenge due to a fundamental dilemma: The large intrinsic energy difference favors the 2H phase, while reducing this difference facilitates 1T formation but thermodynamically promotes mixed phases. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by simultaneously reducing the 2H-1T energy difference and controlling the sign of the magnetic susceptibility difference (Δχ), thereby selectively stabilizing either phase through atomic-scale engineering of isolated ferromagnetic dopants. As a result, we develop a direct, bulk, and cost-effective strategy for the phase-selective synthesis of both 2H and 1T MoS 2 . Experimental characterizations and first-principles calculations reveal that tuning the spacing between isolated dopants coordinately regulates magnetic susceptibility and phase stability, enabling deterministic phase selection. The generality of this strategy is further demonstrated in representative transition metal dichalcogenides. By establishing atomic spacing–engineered magnetic susceptibility as a design principle for polymorph control, this work provides a scalable route to phase-selective synthesis of transition metal dichalcogenides and opens opportunities for single-atom catalysis, magnetoelectronics, and spintronic devices.

articles_hidden.title: Melanocortin-responsive arcuate Kiss1 neurons drive BAT thermogenesis through glutamatergic input to the dorsomedial hypothalamus
articles_hidden.authors: Rajae Talbi, Todd L. Stincic, Nicole Lynch, Encarnacion Torres, Kaitlin Ferrari, Choi Ji Hae, Elizabeth Medve, Karol Walec, Samuel T. Zdon, Sarah Ramírez, Sidney A. Pereira, Carrie E. Mahoney, Martha A. Bosch, Larry Zweifel, Oline K. Rønnekleiv, Rona S. Carroll, Alexander S. Banks, Natalia L. S. Machado, Martin J. Kelly, Víctor M. Navarro
articles_hidden.abstract: The melanocortin system is critical for energy homeostasis, yet our understanding of the circuits through which melanocortin signaling regulates thermogenesis remains incomplete. Here, we identify arcuate Kiss1 (Kiss1 ARC ) neurons as melanocortin-responsive regulators of brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis in male mice. Ablation of Kiss1 ARC neurons induced obesity, while their chemogenetic activation increased BAT thermogenesis without affecting food intake. This increase in BAT thermogenesis is mediated by glutamatergic projections to dorsomedial hypothalamus (DMH) CART/Lepr neurons, which engage the raphe pallidus–BAT pathway. CRISPR-mediated Vglut2 deletion from Kiss1 ARC neurons replicated the obesogenic effect. Deletion of the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene from Kiss1 neurons caused obesity due to increased energy balance. Optogenetic POMC fiber stimulation evoked MC4R-dependent inward currents in Kiss1 neurons. These findings reveal a melanocortin-responsive Kiss1 ARC → DMH circuit that contributes to BAT thermogenesis, establishing Kiss1 neurons as components of the melanocortin pathway beyond their reproductive functions.

articles_hidden.title: Multimodal robotic matter enabled by unified magnetic control primitives
articles_hidden.authors: Konstantinos Manos, Yifan Rao, Tuo Zhao, Minjie Chen, Glaucio H. Paulino
articles_hidden.abstract: Robotic matter seeks to achieve collective functionality through interactions among modular units governed by global control signals. A persistent challenge is identifying control frameworks that are simultaneously scalable and deterministic. Here, we introduce a unified magnetic control paradigm that enables multimodal robotic matter using a minimal set of global-field primitives. We show that combinations of rotating and pulsed uniform fields, together with controlled field gradients, are sufficient to generate diverse behaviors—including multimodal locomotion, deterministic bottom-up assembly, and rapid, reversible shape morphing in origami-inspired modular robots. Each module incorporates permanent magnets with prescribed chirality and magnetic moment, encoding mechanical and magnetic asymmetries that map global field inputs to predictable forces, torques, and deformation pathways. Using a programmable three-dimensional Helmholtz coil system, we demonstrate four locomotion modes (rolling, steering, sliding, and walking), hierarchical assembly of three-dimensional robotic architectures, and millisecond-timescale transitions among discrete stable states, with applications to origami state machines and global shape change for navigation through confined spaces. By unifying locomotion, assembly, and reconfiguration within a single control framework, this work establishes a generalizable approach to magnetic robotic matter in which multifunctional collective behaviors emerge from a minimal set of control primitives.

articles_hidden.title: Mosquito-inspired gentle vibration enhances oral absorption of macromolecular drugs at the mucoadhesive interface
articles_hidden.authors: Chong Zhang, Guangyao Zhao, Yidan Lyu, Runyu Bai, Ningjie Du, Jialu Zhang, Huihui Hu, Hao Song, Junjie Zeng, Yunlong Fan, Tianran Wang, Meng Wang, Qiuju Han, Hien T. T. Duong, Di Wu, Xinge Yu, Kewang Nan
articles_hidden.abstract: Oral administration is convenient, noninvasive, and highly acceptable to patients, yet many polar, hydrophilic, and macromolecular therapeutics remain difficult to deliver efficiently because of poor transport across the intestinal epithelium. Inspired by mosquitoes, which use small-amplitude vibration to reduce tissue resistance during proboscis insertion, we hypothesize that localized, gentle mechanical vibration could provide a gentle and controllable physical strategy to enhance intestinal drug absorption. Here, using an ex vivo intestinal absorption evaluation system, we show that mechanical vibration regulates drug transport in a molecule-dependent manner, selectively enhancing the absorption of strongly polar and hydrophilic drugs and biological macromolecules while reducing tissue transport of drugs with relatively high intrinsic permeability. We further develop a soft oral pill (SOP) that combines magnetic guidance, mucosal adhesion, localized drug release, and externally programmable vibration to promote mechanically assisted transepithelial transport. In diabetic rabbits, vibration-assisted delivery with the SOP achieves a relative oral bioavailability of ∼16% for insulin, ∼16-fold higher than oral insulin administration alone, and induces sustained glucose lowering. This work establishes vibration-assisted mucosal delivery as a minimally invasive and remotely controllable strategy for expanding the oral delivery of poorly absorbed therapeutics.

articles_hidden.title: Physics-embedded neural spectral wave model
articles_hidden.authors: Guangyu Gary Yang, Haoyu Jiang, Wenfang Lu, Dong Wang
articles_hidden.abstract: Simulating ocean surface waves is essential for understanding Earth’s climate and marine environments, but numerical wave models solving directional wave spectrum remain computationally prohibitive for climate applications. Data-driven deep learning approaches struggle to capture wave physics with high dimensionality, failing to generalize beyond their training domains. To bridge this divide, we present the neural spectral wave model (NeuralSWM), a hybrid physics-AI framework. By embedding a differentiable numerical solver to govern universal wave propagation alongside a neural network that learns complex energy source terms, NeuralSWM efficiently simulates full directional wave spectra. The model demonstrates true zero-shot transferability: Trained exclusively on wind-sea dominated semienclosed South China Sea, it can simulate wave dynamics across the swell-dominated Eastern Tropical Pacific and the high-wind, long-fetch regimes of the Southern Indian Ocean. Validated against satellite altimetry, NeuralSWM maintains high accuracy (∼96% of the performance) at a fraction of traditional computational costs, providing a scalable foundation for integrating explicit wave dynamics into global Earth system models.

articles_hidden.title: Global iodine emissions remain near constant over the 21st century
articles_hidden.authors: Ryan J. Pound, Martin R. Wadley, Rosie Chance, David P. Stevens, Mat J. Evans, Lucy J. Carpenter
articles_hidden.abstract: The reaction between atmospheric ozone and ocean iodide releases gaseous iodine into the atmosphere, destroying ozone and nucleating aerosol particles. The current paradigm is that iodine emissions will substantially increase over this century, with implications for climate, air quality, and human health. Using advanced predictions of ocean iodide concentrations and the iodine emissions function, we re-evaluate this understanding. Rather than increasing through 2100, we find minimal change (−3%) in global iodine emissions compared to present day, predominantly due to a sea surface temperature driven decrease in the iodine emissions function together with relatively unchanged sea surface iodide concentrations. However, emissions increases remain in the critical Arctic region (+143%), resulting in an additional 9 ppbv of springtime surface ozone loss across the region. Our results highlight that predictions of future atmospheric iodine depend on the assumed climate-induced changes in oceanic iodide, in addition to changes in emissions driven by anthropogenic ozone and sea-surface temperature.

articles_hidden.title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics
articles_hidden.authors: Ziqi Gao, Ziyi Lu, Yingke Wu, Licheng Han, Yani Xu, Sheng Zhao, Zhijin Tian, Jie Gu, Shiqi Wang, Chenyi Yu, Qi Han, Xinmin Yu, Fang He, Xinyao Yu, Leihao Lu, Jicheng Yu, Yuqi Zhang, Zhen Gu
articles_hidden.abstract: Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

articles_hidden.title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
articles_hidden.authors: Vinh H. Nguyen, Carlos Cruz-Cortés, Joseph O. Primeau, Raelynn Brassard, M. Joanne Lemieux, L. Michel Espinoza-Fonseca, Howard S. Young
articles_hidden.abstract: Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca 2+ -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca 2+ to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca 2+ cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca 2+ -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

articles_hidden.title: Hardware-encoded modality separation for multimodal sensing and artificial perception
articles_hidden.authors: Wooseok Kim, Bosung Kim, Dae Han Kim, Pei Liu, Doyoung Kim, Hee Kyu Lee, Sang Uk Park, Janghoon Joo, Byeong Woon Lee, Se Gi Lee, Bogeun Kim, Jaejun Lim, Changsoon Choi, Jong-Woong Kim, Geumbee Lee, Jae-Young Yoo, Sejin Kim, Joohoon Kang, Raudel Avila, Jong Uk Kim, Sang Min Won
articles_hidden.abstract: Human skin achieves robust perception by distributing modality-specialized receptors that preferentially encode mechanical and thermal cues. Yet, soft and flexible tactile sensors often suffer from cross-sensitivity, where stretching, bending, and temperature variations generate overlapping electrical readouts that undermine reliable multimodal measurement and downstream artificial intelligence–based interpretation. Here, we present a multimodal piezoresistive platform based on doped silicon nanomembranes that leverages their crystallographic anisotropy and a bilayer differential architecture for front-end modality separation. By integrating [110] longitudinal/transverse gauges with [100] reference gauges that exhibit reduced piezoresistive sensitivity but comparable temperature coefficient of resistance, together with a bilayer differential layout, the platform compensates thermal drift and decouples stretching from bending at the hardware level. Experimental and theoretical analyses establish a quantitative framework for separating modality-specific responses under combined stretching, bending, and temperature stimuli. Integrated into a flexible, wireless platform, the decoupled signals enable real-time transmission and deep learning–based interpretation, allowing accurate identification of geometrically similar objects with distinct thermal or mechanical properties. These results highlight the feasibility and need to co-design front-end sensing architectures and learning models to achieve robust, high-accuracy multimodal decoupling in real-world conditions.

articles_hidden.title: Spaceflight reshapes Alzheimer’s disease–associated molecular programs in human brain organoids
articles_hidden.authors: Natalia C. S. Moreira, Luisa B. V. Coelho, Luiz P. Petroski, Stephanie S. Almeida, Luiza P. M. Gaudio, Livia L. Nascimento, Jeong-Hee Lee, Stevens Rehen, Blake Tsu, Juliana de S. da G. Fischer, Paulo C. Carvalho, Aline M. A. Martins, Roberto H. Herai, Alysson R. Muotri
articles_hidden.abstract: Spaceflight provides a unique environment to study neural responses relevant to neurodegenerative diseases. Here, human cortical organoids derived from induced pluripotent stem cells that carry familial Alzheimer’s disease (AD) mutations in APP, PSEN1 , and PSEN2 were cultivated at the International Space Station alongside Controls for 40 days. Multiomic profiling, integrating transcriptomics and proteomics, revealed a coordinated shift in neuronal and cellular states during spaceflight. Spaceflight was associated with changes in amyloid-β processing and tau phosphorylation, although the magnitude of these responses varied across genetic backgrounds. Pathway analysis identified increased synaptic and neurotransmission-related signatures, particularly those associated with GABA-releasing and glutamatergic signaling. Integrative analysis further revealed convergent programs involving RNA processing, chromatin organization, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cellular stress responses. Proteomic and multiomic analyses also identified changes in RNA binding proteins, including CIRBP, consistent with altered posttranscriptional regulatory networks under spaceflight conditions. These exploratory findings indicate that spaceflight reshapes neuronal regulation in human brain organoids, revealing coordinated molecular responses relevant to AD biology.

articles_hidden.title: How far are we from a critical salinity in the North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre?
articles_hidden.authors: Lucas Almeida, Didier Swingedouw
articles_hidden.abstract: The North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre (SPG) can undergo abrupt cooling associated with a loss of deep convection, yet the hydrographic conditions that drive this transition remain uncertain. While some CMIP6 models simulate an abrupt SPG cooling, others do not. Here, we identify a critical sea surface salinity (SSS) that separates these contrasting behaviors. Models without abrupt cooling either remain above this threshold because they project weak freshening or already lie below it under present-day conditions, inconsistent with observations. Observed SSS exceeds the critical threshold by 0.3 to 0.8 g kg −1 , depending on the exact threshold definition. Although no declining trend is currently detected, observations remain consistent with models that simulate abrupt cooling. In these models, SSS begins to decline rapidly and crosses the critical threshold about 20 years after the onset of freshening. These results highlight the importance of sustained salinity observations for detecting the approach to this critical threshold, providing a physically based early warning of an abrupt SPG cooling.

articles_hidden.title: Selenium isotopes uncover the mechanism of the deep plate tectonic cycle in the MORB mantle
articles_hidden.authors: Stephan König, María I. Varas-Reus, Romain Tilhac, Carlos J. Garrido
articles_hidden.abstract: Subduction has recycled oceanic crust into Earth’s interior for billions of years, yet how deeply subducted material evolves and contributes to mantle-derived melts, such as mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORBs), remains poorly resolved. Because subducting slab-derived dehydration fluids typically produce isotopically light selenium (Se) in residual eclogites, which is transferred to mantle melts without further fractionation, Se serves as a powerful isotope-based tracer of recycled components into the mantle. Here, we present high-precision Se isotope data for recycled crust–derived garnet pyroxenites that bridge the gap between the primitive mantle and isotopically lighter MORB. Through two-stage thermodynamic modeling, we trace the reactive infiltration of eclogite-derived melts within the convective mantle, leading to the concurrent formation of subduction-derived garnet pyroxenites that preserve residual eclogite cores, both of which contribute to the mantle source of MORBs during adiabatic decompression. Our results establish a petrologically consistent and isotope-validated framework to trace the fate of subducted crust and its long-term imprint on the MORB mantle throughout the deep plate tectonic cycle.

articles_hidden.title: Stress unmasks disconnected endocrine coordination of glucose metabolism in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
articles_hidden.authors: Gretel S. Major, Cara A. Timpani, Hannah Lalunio, Jiayi Chen, Lauren Boatner, Nicholas Giourmas, Stephanie Kourakis, Eva van den Berg, Ekaterina Salimova, Joel Eliades, Gang Zheng, Rong Xu, Sukhvir Kaur Bhangu, Thirimadura V. H. Mendis, Joel R. Steele, Ralf B. Schittenhelm, Deirdre L. Merry, Louise Lantier, Christoph E. Hagemeyer, Francesca Cavalieri, Karen Caeyenberghs, Aaron P. Russell, Michael de Veer, Craig A. Goodman, Alan Hayes, Emma Rybalka, Charles P. Najt, Angus Lindsay
articles_hidden.abstract: Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using physiological stress to unmask metabolic deficits in the mdx mouse model of DMD, we show that stress hormone signaling rises without an appropriate poststress rise in insulin secretion, maintaining hyperglycemia despite elevated basal glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Rather than reflecting increased gluconeogenesis, this hyperglycemia appears to stem from impaired glucose oxidative disposal; skeletal muscle stores glucose as glycogen instead of oxidizing it, while the heart and brain show persistent, tissue-specific uptake differences. Restoring insulin availability transiently corrects glucose control and reverses stress-induced deficits. Instead of correcting glucose handling, removing excess glucose directly using empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) prevents stress-induced increases in blood glucose. These findings identify a breakdown in endocrine-metabolic coordination underlying metabolic vulnerability in DMD and demonstrate two mechanistically distinct routes, restoring insulin secretion or bypassing it entirely, to restore metabolic resilience under stress.

articles_hidden.title: A precipitation threshold delineates contrasting controls on global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization
articles_hidden.authors: Wenqi Jiao, Tao Hu, Chongchong Qi, Liyuan Chai
articles_hidden.abstract: Nitrogen fertilization is a major driver of soil acidification globally, yet its independent effects on soil pH and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly resolved. Here we isolate the contribution of nitrogen fertilization by compiling the largest paired experimental dataset to date, consisting of 3564 paired soil pH observations under control and nitrogen fertilization treatments across seven major ecosystem types worldwide. By constructing robust machine-learning models, we predict global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization (pH_T) and quantify fertilization-associated pH change under a standardized hypothetical fertilization scenario. Under this scenario, we estimate that 96.27% of global soils undergo acidification, with a mean pH decline of 0.34 units. Critically, we identify a precipitation threshold at ∼900 mm year −1 that separates two distinct regimes in the relationship between precipitation and pH_T: climate-driven leaching and buffering in drier regions versus soil-mediated internal regulation in humid regions. This threshold demonstrates that the association between precipitation and pH_T is not uniform across the global precipitation gradient but varies markedly among hydroclimatic regions. Our results provide a global outlook on soil pH responses to nitrogen fertilization, supporting acidification risk early warning, precision fertilizer management, and sustainable agricultural development.

articles_hidden.title: Spectral dynamics reservoir computing: High-performance neuromorphic computation from coarse spectra
articles_hidden.authors: Jiaxuan Chen, Ryo Iguchi, Sota Hikasa, Takashi Tsuchiya
articles_hidden.abstract: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) uses material dynamics to perform non–von Neumann neuromorphic computation, yet how to exploit information in the materials remains critical for advancing real-time practical applications. Although many physical materials intrinsically exhibit nonlinear oscillatory dynamics whose frequency-domain features have been shown to support powerful neuromorphic computation, accessing this information at high processing speeds yields only coarse spectra due to the time-frequency trade-off. Here, we present spectral dynamics reservoir computing (SDRC), a framework based on selective filtering and envelope detection, which leverages coarse spectra of material responses to achieve high-speed, high-performance computation with hardware-efficient implementation. We experimentally demonstrate SDRC applied to spin waves using passive analog filters and diodes. Our system achieves strong benchmark performance and 98.0% accuracy in real-world speech recognition without cochleagram preprocessing, substantially reducing the required number of readout channels while outperforming conventional time-multiplexing approaches. Our work establishes a hardware-efficient framework for harnessing high-speed spectral dynamics in computation, paving the way for real-time neuromorphic processors.

articles_hidden.title: Whole-plant visualization of endogenous RNA with an RNA-sensing fluorescence reporter toward single-molecule imaging
articles_hidden.authors: Jiuyuan Bai, Jiayu Zhang, Hongpei Ren, Shan Pan, Yiran Tao, Miaomiao Lei, Mengyue Dong, Sha Liu, Jia Yi, Fang Chen, Yucheng Shen, Yazhou Chen, Jiang Li, Chunhai Fan, Yun Zhao
articles_hidden.abstract: Spatiotemporal mapping of endogenous RNA expression and trafficking in living plants remains challenging. Here, we introduce the plant endogenous RNA reporting system (PERS), an RNA-sensing fluorescent platform for in vivo visualization of unmodified native transcripts. PERS integrates an engineered target-binding allosteric RNA switch that sterically shields a miniature degron on a modular green fluorescent protein reporter, coupled with a SunTag-based signal amplification module. This design enables noninvasive, single molecule–sensitive imaging of plant endogenous RNAs with substantially improved signal-to-background performance, without detectable perturbation to plant growth or tested target-gene expression. Using PERS, we resolved subcellular localization and trafficking of individual RNAs and quantitatively tracked gene expression dynamics from single cells to whole plants across multiple contexts, including constitutive housekeeping genes, tissue-specific expression patterns, circadian rhythm oscillations, and acute stress-responsive programs. By enabling programmable, high-specificity detection of endogenous RNAs across scales, PERS provides a platform to map RNA localization and trafficking in vivo, opening avenues to dissect and engineer systemic signaling networks in plant biology.

articles_hidden.title: Visual learning through auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep
articles_hidden.authors: Musi Xie, Zhuoqun Li, Yuxin Fan, Yifan Li, Xingbei Wan, Sirui Yang, Shiman Huang, Chengsi Zhao, Ning Ma, Fang Fang, Xilin Zhang
articles_hidden.abstract: Visual learning, like other kinds of learning, has classically been attributed to intensive, active training; however, whether it can be achieved via effortless, passive reactivation remains unresolved. Here, we triggered targeted reactivation using auditory tones that had acquired contextual meaning through preceding visual–auditory associative learning. Re-exposure to learned tones improved subsequent visual performance during both wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. Wake reactivation matched training in both improvement and improvement per trial, whereas sleep reactivation surpassed both wake reactivation and training. By contrast, re-exposure to unlearned tones impaired performance only during slow-wave sleep. Reactivation-induced improvement and impairment were strictly orientation- and location-specific and were associated with a convergent auditory–visual coupling pathway. Beyond this shared pathway, auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep unfolded through distinct coupling architectures linking sensory and higher-order cortical regions. Collectively, our findings establish auditory reactivation as a highly efficient route to visual learning, identify sleep as its most potent state, and reveal a double-edged, state-dependent neuroplastic architecture.

articles_hidden.title: Historical evidence that wildfire frequency modulates debris-flow hazards through sediment-supply limitation
articles_hidden.authors: Emily C. Geyman, Michael P. Lamb
articles_hidden.abstract: Southern California is an epicenter of postwildfire debris flows. In this region, steep topography, frequent fire, heavy rainstorms, and large populations along the wildland-urban interface conspire to produce costly debris flows. Wildfire frequency in the region has tripled in recent decades, causing concern about escalating debris-flow hazards. Here, we investigate how wildfire frequency affects the magnitude of postfire erosion by analyzing long-term debris basin records. We identify two contrasting erosional styles. In steep catchments, erosion exhibits a binge-purge behavior: Erosion for 3 years following fire exceeds background rates by ∼17×. In contrast, in low-sloping, soil-mantled catchments, sediment export following fire only exceeds background rates by ∼1.5×. Critically, in the steep catchments, debris-flow volumes decline when wildfires recur more frequently than the ∼30-year interval characteristic of the past century. This observation suggests a sediment-supply limitation in which more frequent wildfire may reduce, rather than amplify, some of Southern California’s most severe debris-flow hazards.

articles_hidden.title: Dual- q chirality from chirality-polarity coupling in polar nematic fluids
articles_hidden.authors: Luyao Sun, Yu Zou, Yang Ding, Jidan Yang, Xiang Huang, Mingjun Huang, Yanqing Lu, Bingxiang Li, Satoshi Aya
articles_hidden.abstract: Tuning delicate polar domain structures with chirality offers a promising route to exploring emergent states in condensed-matter physics. Here, we report the emergence of counterintuitive dual- q chirality and its tunability in domain structures of chiral ferroelectric fluids with nematic order. The dual- q chiral domains are composed of asymmetric twisting wave numbers (or wavelengths) in neighboring twisted domains, in contrast to the common understanding that a single system with a specific chirality favors only one wavelength of helix. This dual- q chirality arises from the formation of periodic twist polar domains with opposite chiral signs to reduce electrostatic energy, while the different twisting wave numbers of the helices in neighboring domains balance the chiral and electrostatic energies. We observe a crossover with inherent hysteresis from an electrostatics-dominant to a chirality-dominant region, triggering a transition from a dual- q chiral to a homo -chiral state.

articles_hidden.title: Meridional ocean temperature gradient drives climate stability in the Late Ordovician
articles_hidden.authors: Joseph Naar, Yannick Donnadieu, Alexandre Pohl, Guillaume Le Hir, Jean-Baptiste Ladant, Daniel J. Lunt
articles_hidden.abstract: The Hirnantian glaciation (Late Ordovician, 445 million years ago) involved rapid tropical cooling of ∼7°C, difficult to reproduce without invoking a major decline in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). A previous modeling study provided an appealing explanation by identifying a climatic instability in the Late Ordovician ocean-atmosphere system using the Fast Ocean Atmosphere Model (FOAM), whereby a modest decrease in atmospheric partial pressure of CO 2 ( P co 2 ) triggered abrupt tropical cooling. Here, our simulations with the comprehensive IPSL-CM5A2 model instead show continuous cooling as P co 2 decreases. We attribute this contrasting behavior to the warmer high-latitude climate simulated by FOAM, which predisposes sea ice to an abrupt transition and arises from overly diffusive ocean dynamics and coupled cloud radiative processes. Yet, broader model intercomparison suggests that climate stability is controlled by the equator-to-pole temperature gradient, rather than by model realism or complexity. These findings have major implications for constraining the onset and evolution of the Hirnantian glaciation, by exploiting proxy-constrained meridional temperature gradients and contrasting model parameterizations as physically motivated end-member hypotheses.

articles_hidden.title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori
articles_hidden.authors: Wenhuang Ban, Min Sun, Jingjing Qu, Yuening Zhong, Weixi Wu, Yijun Lin, Yu Liu, Runqin Tan, Xiumei Ni, Song Zhou, Shan Guan, Dan Shao, Yan He, Kaiyun Liu, Chengzhong Yu, Jie Tang
articles_hidden.abstract: Helicobacter pylori infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

articles_hidden.title: Embodied mechanical sensing through self-generated motion in climbing plants
articles_hidden.authors: Amir Ohad, Amir Porat, Yasmine Meroz
articles_hidden.abstract: Embodied mechanical intelligence and morphological computation enable adaptive behavior by shifting computation from centralized control to body mechanics. However, how dynamical material structures encode environmental information remains poorly understood. Here, we address this question using twining plants as a minimal decentralized system. Combining force measurements with physical modeling, we show that circumnutating shoots generate predictable forces against candidate supports and that the interaction is equivalent to a rotating cantilever governed by torque balance. Force amplitude is determined by stem stiffness and geometry, while the timescale is set by circumnutation rate. Twining occurs only after reaching a critical torque threshold, corresponding to a deformation that reflects support stability and geometric reach. Motorized perturbations further show that twining timescales inversely with effective circumnutation rate. Together, these results show how self-generated motion extracts actionable information about the environment, while the tapered geometry and spatially varying mechanics of the shoot encode the decision-making threshold for attachment.

articles_hidden.title: Nanos remodels Drosophila germ granules into multiphase condensates for germ cell specification
articles_hidden.authors: Kwan Yin Lee, Harathi Jonnagaddala, Marcus D. Kilwein, Akira Nakamura, Marian Kalocsay, Elizabeth R. Gavis
articles_hidden.abstract: Biomolecular condensates assemble, remodel, and disassemble in response to changing cellular conditions, but the mechanisms that drive these transitions remain poorly understood. Germ granules—RNA-rich condensates essential for germ cell development and fertility—exhibit developmental plasticity, yet how this behavior is controlled is not known. Using in situ proximity labeling, quantitative proteomics, and live super-resolution imaging, we show that Drosophila germ granules are remodeled into multiphasic condensates after primordial germ cell formation. Remodeling is driven by the conserved RNA binding protein Nanos, translated from germ granule–localized nanos messenger RNA (mRNA). As Nanos accumulates above a critical threshold, it condenses to form a coat surrounding the germ granules and recruits the CCR4-Not deadenylase complex and other P-body components. Transition to this hybrid germ granule–P-body–like state alters condensate organization and physical properties. Formation of the Nanos coat coincides with the release of nanos mRNA from germ granules while promoting the retention and relocalization of Cyclin B mRNA from the granule interior to the Nanos phase. These findings identify an autoregulatory developmental timer in which Nanos drives condensate remodeling to control the localization and fate of its own and other mRNAs during germ cell specification.

articles_hidden.title: Unseen but not unheard: Animal-borne audio recorders reveal missing interactions between seabirds and untracked vessels
articles_hidden.authors: Jonathan D. Rutter, Sarah Bond, Ana P.B. Carneiro, Aline da Silva Cerqueira, Igor Debski, Johannes H. Fischer, Robin Freeman, Dave Goad, Louise Maurice, Jason Moss, Oliver Padget, Olivia Rowley, Kate Simister, Graeme Taylor, Stephen C. Votier, Katrina J. Davis, Tim Guilford
articles_hidden.abstract: Quantifying interactions between marine megafauna and vessels is key to assessing the ecological impacts of commercial fishing and shipping. Automatic identification systems (AIS), by publicly tracking global vessel activities, have enabled animal-vessel interactions to be identified at scale. However, the extent of these interactions is inevitably underestimated due to “unseen” vessels that lack AIS or have gaps in coverage from technical issues or intentional disabling. Using animal-borne audio recorders on three seabird species (northern gannet, Balearic shearwater, and Westland petrel), we investigated whether acoustic detection of vessel sounds could reveal a more complete picture of interactions. We found that a striking proportion of vessel audio detections (gannets, >32%, estimated 57%; shearwaters, >12%, estimated 20%) could not be matched with AIS-tracked vessels, suggesting substantial potential for bycatch risk from unseen fishing. Our approach is computationally lightweight, applicable to pre-existing datasets, and transferrable to non-seabird taxa. Acoustic detection could improve future assessments of animal-vessel interactions and unseen vessel activities to support marine conservation.

articles_hidden.title: Arctic forcing of European spring productivity and agricultural yields linked to Barents Sea ice loss
articles_hidden.authors: Zhi Huang, Jun Wang, Philippe Ciais, Xichen Li, William K. M. Lau, Ning Zeng, Wenping Yuan, Haijin Dai, Hao Zhou, Jinfeng Ding, Meirong Wang, Ran Yan, Duwei Zhong, Anmin Duan, Yimin Liu, Jing M. Chen, Fei Jiang, Weimin Ju
articles_hidden.abstract: Arctic sea ice loss reshapes midlatitude climate, yet its cascading impacts on terrestrial carbon cycling and food security remain unclear. Barents Sea ice area (BSIA) has experienced the Arctic’s fastest decline. Using four decades of satellite observations, agricultural statistics, and Earth system model (ESM) simulations, we identify late-winter BSIA as a key driver of European spring productivity. Interannual BSIA reductions substantially enhance gross primary productivity (GPP) and raise national wheat yields by up to 16.5% in Eastern Europe, a global breadbasket. Reanalysis and model experiments reveal that reduced BSIA alters large-scale circulation through stratosphere-troposphere coupling, wave–mean flow interactions, and Rossby wave propagation. Anomalous subsidence drives adiabatic and radiative warming; cyclonic flow strengthens warm-air advection, together alleviating thermal constraints on photosynthesis. Although most ESMs capture atmospheric teleconnections, they systematically underestimate productivity responses due to underrepresented GPP-temperature sensitivity. BSIA decline accounts for approximately half of the four-decade increase in Eastern European productivity, highlighting an overlooked Arctic forcing of midlatitude carbon dynamics.

articles_hidden.title: Continuously aligned biomimetic sites in MXene membranes for rapid lithium extraction
articles_hidden.authors: Zihan Liu, Longfeng Hu, Sijin Li, Shirong Li, Tianhuai Kang, Hongzhi Liu, Gaoxin Dai, Langming Bai, Heng Liang
articles_hidden.abstract: Efficient separation of lithium ions (Li + ) from magnesium ions (Mg 2+ ) remains a central challenge for direct lithium extraction from salt lake brines due to their similar physicochemical properties. Inspired by biological ion channels, biomimetic membranes have been explored to improve Li + /Mg 2+ separation. However, most biomimetic membranes focus primarily on introducing recognition sites while overlooking the structural features of biological channels, particularly the continuous arrangement of coordination sites that facilitates efficient ion transport. Here, inspired by the continuous carbonyl coordination structure of the KcsA ion channel, 4-formylbenzo-15-crown-5 ether was periodically grafted onto poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) chains and integrated with MXene nanosheets to construct two-dimensional interlayer channels with continuously aligned crown ether recognition sites. This architecture shifts Li + transport from random diffusion to successive site-to-site hopping, reducing the effective transport energy barrier. The resulting biomimetic MXene membrane achieves a Li + flux of 0.12 mol·m −2 ·h −1 with Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of 109 and performs effectively across various salt lake brines.

articles_hidden.title: Functional buffering potential of generalist-rich microbiomes is associated with coral thermotolerance
articles_hidden.authors: Chuanzhu Bai, Jian Zhang, Lei Jiang, Pan Zhang, Si Zhang, Hui Huang, Jie Li
articles_hidden.abstract: Climate change threatens coral reefs globally, highlighting the need to understand mechanisms underlying coral holobiont resilience. Intertidal corals exhibit superior heat tolerance, yet the role of associated microbiomes remains unclear. By integrating field surveys, heat-stress experiments, and metagenomics, we compared intertidal and subtidal Porites lutea microbiomes. Our results show that intertidal P. lutea host bacterial communities are enriched in generalists with broad niche breadths and exhibit high functional redundancy in stress-response pathways. Under acute thermal stress, intertidal corals showed greater thermotolerance than subtidal corals. Concurrently, intertidal coral-associated bacterial communities maintained relatively stable taxonomic composition and functional integrity. Across habitats, preservation of photosynthetic efficiency ( F v / F m ) in the coral holobiont under heat stress was associated with higher bacterial generalist richness and functional redundancy. Together, these results suggest that long-term environmental variability may be associated with microbiome features consistent with functional buffering and holobiont stability. These findings may inform the design of synthetic microbial consortia to improve coral resilience under warming oceans.

articles_hidden.title: Ultra-generalized hologram synthesis via domain-adaptive wavefront learning
articles_hidden.authors: Runze Zhu, Jiasheng Xiao, Hao Zhang, Hong-Bo Sun
articles_hidden.abstract: Deep learning–based computer-generated holography is essential for creating lifelike three-dimensional (3D) visuals in extended reality and immersive human-digital interaction. However, current data-driven approaches predominantly rely on a 3D-solution search strategy that couples scene representation with physical parameters. This paradigm leads to physical overfitting, restricting models to fixed wavelengths and depths and preventing generalization across diverse 3D data formats. Here, we report a 2D-solution search technique, wavefront-aware neural encoding (WNE). This method is a universal framework that overcomes these limitations via domain-adaptive wavefront learning. By compensating for feature distribution shifts induced by varying data formats and physical parameters, WNE maps various wavefronts into a unified feature domain compatible with a frozen, pretrained encoder. This mechanism enables ultra-generalized hologram synthesis: A single pretrained network can encode high-fidelity phase-only holograms for diverse 3D representations, from conventional layer-based data to emerging Gaussian splatting. Outperforming previous analytical and neural encoding methods in image quality, WNE establishes a robust, plug-and-play engine for diverse holographic applications.

articles_hidden.title: TREX1 and TREX2 3′ → 5′ DNA exonucleases enhance the fidelity of translesion synthesis by DNA polymerase θ
articles_hidden.authors: Jung-Hoon Yoon, Karthi Sellamuthu, Louise Prakash, Satya Prakash
articles_hidden.abstract: A multiplicity of translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerases (Pols) promote replication through DNA lesions in an error-free or error-prone manner. Among these Pols, Polθ operates in an error-prone manner. However, Polθ conducts TLS in human cells in a much more error-free manner than implicated from the high error-proneness of the purified Pol. To resolve this incongruity, here we show that the TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonucleases are integral components of TLS mediated by Polθ. In TREX1- or TREX2-deficient cells, Polθ-dependent TLS becomes nonoperational and chromosomal instability rises similar to that in Polθ-deficient cells. Consequently, similar to that in Polθ −/− mice, trex2 −/− mice exhibit increased susceptibility to ultraviolet-induced skin cancers. Furthermore, our findings that in the absence of TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonuclease activities, Polθ-mediated TLS manifests high mutagenicity, and an increase in the diversity of misincorporated nucleotides demarcate a crucial role of these exonucleases in the removal of Polθ misinsertions and, thereby, in enhancing Polθ TLS fidelity and the consequent genome stability.

articles_hidden.title: Drug candidate CT7-1 promotes antitumor immunity by targeting SETMAR to activate cGAS-STING-IFN signaling in breast cancer
articles_hidden.authors: Jian Chen, Kaiyuan Ji, Dong Chen, Weiye Pan, Chengkuan Liu, Meng Liu, Junlin Qian, Junchang Huang, Yuwei Peng, Cheng Tao, Xian Lin
articles_hidden.abstract: The discovery of previously unidentified anti–breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8 + T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)–mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell–mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

articles_hidden.title: Uterine-derived anisotropic compressive force specifies the anterior-posterior axis orientation in the mouse embryo
articles_hidden.authors: Seiya Mikoshiba, Hiroshi Koyama, Sanae Oka, Takaya Abe, Hiroshi Kiyonari, Masahiko Hibi, Toshihiko Fujimori
articles_hidden.abstract: The establishment of the anterior-posterior (A-P) axis is a fundamental process in embryonic patterning. In mice, directional migration of the anterior visceral endoderm (AVE) determines the A-P axis, yet the cues directing migration remain elusive. Here, we show that anisotropic compression directs AVE migration toward the minor-axis end of the deformed embryo, using ex utero culture with controlled compression and in utero pharmacological manipulations of uterine mechanics. This compression induces localized accumulation of basement membrane (BM) components, including COLLAGEN IV, which directs the AVE toward the minor-axis end. Mathematical modeling demonstrates that BM density-dependent AVE-BM adhesion accounts for the observed AVE dynamics. Our findings reveal that the maternal mechanical environment provides directional cues for cell migration, bridging tissue-scale mechanics and biochemical patterning during body axis specification.

articles_hidden.title: Oligodendrocyte ER-phagy restricts excessive myelination by degrading sphingolipid synthases
articles_hidden.authors: Tingxin Zhang, Daniela Barbosa, Aksheev Bhambri, Lu O. Sun
articles_hidden.abstract: Myelination is critical for nervous system function. Numerous signaling pathways have been identified that promote myelin sheath growth, disruption of which can lead to hypomyelination. However, the negative regulators of myelin sheath expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–phagy as a cellular brake on central nervous system myelination that restricts myelin sheath thickness during brain development. ER-phagy is active in oligodendrocytes during myelin membrane expansion and limits the abundance of ER-resident sphingolipid synthases, including ceramide synthase 2 (Cers2). Impairment of ER-phagy accumulates ER, elevates sphingolipid production, drives excessive myelin thickening, and alters social behavior after prolonged juvenile social isolation. Genetic deletion of Cers2, which synthesizes long-chain ceramides essential for sphingolipid biogenesis, rescues the hypermyelination phenotype caused by ER-phagy disruption. Together, our findings establish that ER-phagy–sphingolipid axis represses myelin growth and reveal a mechanistic link between ER homeostasis and myelin production by oligodendrocytes, providing insight into the cellular mechanisms underlying pathological hypermyelination.
